item.title: Czech PM Babis suffers setback in Senate elections
item.description: Leading Czech opposition parties won the most votes in Senate elections on Saturday, while Prime Minister Andrej Babis' party failed to secure any of the seats it contested in one of its first big electoral tests since taking power last year.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Leading Czech opposition parties won the most votes in Senate elections on Saturday, while Prime Minister Andrej Babis' party failed to secure any of the seats it contested in one of its first big electoral tests since taking power last year. Babis' ANO party had hoped to make gains in the 81-seat upper house, where one-third of seats were up for election and opposition parties hold a majority. Babis described the result as "catastrophic", but the outcome is unlikely to destabilise his eurosceptic coalition government, which includes right-wing and far-right parties. Since taking office, the government has ended direct state military support for Ukraine in its war with Russia and challenged European Union climate policies. The lower house remains the country's main legislative chamber and can override Senate vetoes, limiting the upper chamber's ability to block government legislation. The Senate nevertheless plays an important role in approving constitutional changes, confirming presidential nominees to the Constitutional Court and electing its own speaker, the country's second-highest state official after the president. Despite the setback, ANO continues to lead national opinion polls. The government has loosened fiscal policy to boost wages, pensions and transport investment, drawing criticism in the traditionally frugal country of 10.9 million people. Turnout in run-off voting for Senate seats on Friday and Saturday was low, following the first round last weekend. Under the electoral system, the top two candidates advance to a run-off unless one secures more than 50% of the vote in the first round. The pro-European Mayors and Independents party emerged as the strongest performer, winning 10 of the 14 seats it contested, including two secured outright in the first round. The Civic Democrats won seven seats. The vote followed municipal elections last weekend in which ANO won six of the country's 13 regional capitals, down from eight four years ago.

item.title: Cofundador da Anthropic afirma que impacto da IA acelera rapidamente e pode impulsionar PIB dos EUA
item.description: O rápido avanço das capacidades da inteligência artificial trará mudanças muito mais rápidas em todas as áreas, afirmou neste sábado o cofundador da Anthropic, Jack Clark, com um dos modelos econômicos internos da empresa prevendo que isso poderia ampliar significativamente a produção econômica dos EUA para US$44 trilhões até 2030.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O rápido avanço das capacidades da inteligência artificial trará mudanças muito mais rápidas em todas as áreas, afirmou neste sábado o cofundador da Anthropic, Jack Clark, com um dos modelos econômicos internos da empresa prevendo que isso poderia ampliar significativamente a produção econômica dos EUA para US$44 trilhões até 2030. Em discurso nas reuniões anuais do FMI e do Banco Mundial em Bangcoc, Clark disse que é necessária uma cooperação internacional para estabelecer “regras incomuns e rigorosas” para essa tecnologia transformadora. Clark disse que o número de US$44 trilhões, que se compara ao nível atual de pouco mais de US$30 trilhões, “parece muito absurdo”, mas a IA está aumentando enormemente as descobertas científicas. “Eu sei, mas isso decorre da premissa de que a tecnologia continuará melhorando. E se o PIB crescesse tanto assim, a doutrina econômica sugere que novas indústrias e invenções precisariam ter sido criadas para impulsionar uma expansão econômica tão significativa.” (Reportagem de David Lawder)

item.title: Aerolíneas recortan vuelos a Tulum, a medida que los turistas abandonan ese paraíso festivo de México
item.description: Si bien los elevados costes del combustible, la apreciación del peso, la violencia de las bandas y las graves proliferaciones de algas invasoras han lastrado el turismo en los destinos de playa mexica ...
item.dc:creator: Andrea Navarro, Valentine Hilaire
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — American Airlines Group Inc. ( AAL ) se ha convertido en la tercera gran aerolínea en otras tantas semanas en recortar sus vuelos a la localidad mexicana de Tulum, ya que la caída del turismo en uno de los destinos caribeños tradicionalmente más populares del país está llevando a los inversores a buscar formas de recuperar su ambiente de élite. La aerolínea estadounidense reducirá su servicio en el aeropuerto de Tulum como parte de una reducción más amplia de la capacidad de la terminal, según informó American el jueves en un comunicado a Bloomberg. El 30 de septiembre, Grupo Aeroméxico SAB suspendió sus vuelos a Tulum y Controladora Vuela Cia de Aviación SAB, conocida como Volaris, anunció que tiene previsto hacer lo mismo a principios del próximo año. La reducción de los vuelos y su impacto económico cobrarán protagonismo cuando dé comienzo este domingo en Ciudad de México la cumbre de aviación de la Asociación Latinoamericana y del Caribe de Transporte Aéreo. Ver más : El triste declive de Tulum es una advertencia para México Las aerolíneas estadounidenses están reduciendo drásticamente su oferta, recortando la capacidad con destino a Tulum en un 72% para este trimestre, según el analista de Bloomberg Intelligence, François Duflot. American ha indicado que pondrá fin a su servicio desde Miami, pero que seguirá operando su ruta desde Dallas. Si bien los elevados costes del combustible, la apreciación del peso, la violencia de las bandas y las graves proliferaciones de algas invasoras han lastrado el turismo en los destinos de playa mexicanos en general, Tulum está sufriendo más que otros destinos. La capacidad de Tulum se ha reducido aproximadamente a la mitad para esta temporada, lo que supone un marcado contraste con la vecina Cancún, donde la reducción es de solo un 3 %. “Sin duda, la débil demanda influye, ya que los consumidores estadounidenses probablemente estén revisando sus planes de viaje a medida que la inflación sigue mermando su poder adquisitivo”, señaló Duflot. “La diferencia entre los dos aeropuertos demuestra que la débil demanda de viajes no es el único factor y que Tulum no ha logrado imponerse frente a Cancún”. El aeropuerto, inaugurado en diciembre de 2023 bajo el mandato del expresidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador, se construyó para dar servicio a 5,5 millones de pasajeros al año como puerta de entrada al sureste de México. Sin embargo, la demanda hacia esas localidades no ha estado a la altura de las expectativas. La presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum restó importancia la semana pasada a las preocupaciones sobre la caída del turismo, señalando el regreso de los vuelos de temporada a Tulum desde Canadá y Estados Unidos, el servicio adicional de la aerolínea estatal y los esfuerzos por mejorar el acceso a los yacimientos arqueológicos de la localidad. Atribuyó la retirada de Aeroméxico al aumento de los costes del combustible y a decisiones empresariales. Tulum, incluso antes de la construcción del aeropuerto, corría el riesgo de crecer demasiado y demasiado rápido. La deficiente infraestructura, la construcción excesiva y los precios abusivos habían mermado su atractivo. La infraestructura no logró seguir el ritmo del auge pospandémico, que vio cómo los nómadas digitales acudían en masa a esta playa caribeña, ya que allí había pocas restricciones pandémicas. Antes de ese auge, el destino atraía principalmente a un público reducido y adinerado, según Ignacio García, un argentino que lleva ocho años viviendo allí. “No solo veía a famosos, sino que estaba con ellos”, afirmó, recordando las visitas de Cardi B y Alicia Keys. La desaceleración también ha afectado a los hoteles. La ocupación en Tulum se situó en una media del 63,7% en los primeros siete meses de 2026, frente al 72,7 % del año anterior, según la Secretaría de Turismo de Quintana Roo. Algunos hoteleros e inversores ven esta desaceleración como una oportunidad para alejarse del turismo de masas, centrado en la fiesta, y recuperar el destino exclusivo y de alta gama que, según ellos, Tulum siempre estuvo destinado a ser. La apuesta por el ‘Tulum 3.0′ va más allá de los nuevos complejos turísticos, ya que busca sacar partido de las tendencias de bienestar y lujo, imitando el ambiente de destinos de élite como Aspen, en Estados Unidos, y Miconos, en Grecia. Por ejemplo, la promotora mexicana Inmobilia está construyendo un complejo hotelero y residencial de lujo bajo la marca Faena en Tulum, mientras que UMusic Hospitality & Lifestyle, respaldada por Universal Music Group, se prepara para inaugurar un hotel de 57 habitaciones en diciembre. La recesión también está redefiniendo la situación económica para los visitantes que permanecen más tiempo. Angelika Pokovba, una estadounidense de 30 años que trabaja a distancia desde Ciudad de México, mantiene un segundo apartamento en el barrio de La Veleta, en Tulum, desde 2020. Su alquiler mensual ha bajado un 40%, hasta los MXN$15.000 (US$811), ya que los propietarios han rebajado los precios para retener a los inquilinos, lo que la ha ayudado a decidirse a seguir renovando el contrato de alquiler. Sin embargo, la reducción de la oferta de vuelos podría cambiar esa ecuación. Pokovba señaló que, si la disminución de los vuelos provoca un aumento de las tarifas aéreas, mantener el apartamento podría dejar de tener sentido desde el punto de vista económico. Ver más: Fotos: Estos son los hoteles más bellos del mundo en 2026 y uno en México sobresale --Con la colaboración de Sri Taylor. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: Membros do FMI pedem mais apoio em meio a impactos de guerras e a riscos da “inteligência avançada”
item.description: Os países membros do Fundo Monetário Internacional (FMI) pediram um aumento do apoio aos países que enfrentam desafios de financiamento de curto prazo causados por repercussões negativas decorrentes de guerras e dos altos preços da energia, e afirmaram que os riscos econômicos continuam inclinados para o lado negativo.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder
item.content:encoded: Os países membros do Fundo Monetário Internacional (FMI) pediram um aumento do apoio aos países que enfrentam desafios de financiamento de curto prazo causados por repercussões negativas decorrentes de guerras e dos altos preços da energia, e afirmaram que os riscos econômicos continuam inclinados para o lado negativo. E, embora tenha havido um impulso aos investimentos e ao comércio por meio das “tecnologias de inteligência avançada”, elas também acarretam riscos, afirmou o presidente do Comitê Monetário e Financeiro Internacional em um comunicado após uma reunião em Bangcoc. “A escalada de conflitos e tensões comerciais pode perturbar ainda mais rotas comerciais essenciais, agravar as pressões sobre os preços das commodities, inclusive dos produtos energéticos refinados, e piorar a segurança energética e alimentar”, afirmou o comunicado divulgado pelo ministro das Finanças da Arábia Saudita, Mohammed Al-Jadaan, presidente do IMFC. O IMFC é o principal comitê diretor do fundo de crédito para crises, que conta com 191 membros. Al-Jadaan disse à Reuters que o texto do comunicado foi acordado por todos os membros. No início desta semana, os Estados Unidos estavam pressionando outros membros do FMI para que renomeassem a inteligência artificial como “superinteligência” no comunicado, em consonância com o nome preferido pelo presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, para a tecnologia, disse uma [USN:L1N4610GV TEXT:"autoridade de alto escalão do Tesouro dos EUA à Reuters"]. A versão final da declaração do presidente do IMFC não continha nenhuma referência à inteligência artificial. A declaração afirmou que o impacto incerto das “tecnologias de inteligência avançada”, juntamente com a alta dos rendimentos dos títulos nas principais economias, que se transmite para países com elevado endividamento, "pode ampliar as vulnerabilidades macrofinanceiras". “As rápidas mudanças tecnológicas, as transformações demográficas, a maior frequência de eventos climáticos extremos e desastres naturais, bem como a fragmentação geoeconômica, estão agravando os dilemas de política pública”, afirmava a declaração. As economias membros concordaram em apoiar os países que empreendem reformas e lidam com vulnerabilidades relacionadas à dívida, com atenção especial aos países de baixa renda e de renda média vulneráveis, bem como aos Estados afetados por conflitos. “Incentivamos o aumento do apoio a países com dívida sustentável e uma agenda sólida de reformas e promoção do crescimento, mas que enfrentam desafios de financiamento de curto prazo”, afirma o comunicado, observando que vários membros garantiram apoio ao Fundo de Redução da Pobreza e Crescimento do FMI, que apoia países pobres e em desenvolvimento. (Reportagem de David Lawder)

item.title: Los trabajadores de Antofagasta pondrán fin a la huelga, lo que aliviará las tensiones en torno al cobre en Chile
item.description: El acuerdo se produce pocos días después de que más de 1.000 supervisores y empleados de Escondida, del Grupo BHP, aceptaran un acuerdo de última hora que evitó una huelga en la mina de cobre más gran ...
item.dc:creator: James Attwood
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Los trabajadores de la mina de cobre Centinela, propiedad de Antofagasta Plc en Chile, votaron el sábado a favor de aceptar una nueva oferta salarial, lo que supone el fin de una huelga que amenazaba con interrumpir la producción en un momento de escasez de suministro a nivel mundial. Los miembros de los dos sindicatos que llevaban en huelga desde el 7 de octubre aprobaron la última propuesta de Antofagasta, según informó un responsable sindical a través de mensajes de texto. Una vez firmados los convenios, la huelga daría por concluida. Ver más : Protesta en mina de cobre de Antofagasta en Chile se intensifica con huelga de hambre El acuerdo se produce pocos días después de que más de 1.000 supervisores y empleados de Escondida, del Grupo BHP, aceptaran un acuerdo de última hora que evitó una huelga en la mina de cobre más grande del mundo. Ambos acuerdos alivian las preocupaciones sobre las interrupciones en el suministro, justo cuando los productores se esfuerzan por seguir el ritmo de la creciente demanda. El fin de la huelga de Centinela elimina un quebradero de cabeza para la industria del cobre chilena, aunque aún quedan muchos por resolver. La producción en el principal país productor se ha visto afectada por accidentes, condiciones meteorológicas adversas y contratiempos operativos, lo que ha contribuido a la escasez de la oferta mundial. Al mismo tiempo, la amenaza de los aranceles está atrayendo el metal hacia los almacenes estadounidenses, mientras que la demanda de cobre utilizado en redes eléctricas y centros de datos se está disparando, con el metal cotizando cerca de máximos históricos. Los dos sindicatos de Centinela, que representan a unos 700 trabajadores, iniciaron la huelga después de que las negociaciones colectivas habituales no lograran resolver las diferencias sobre salarios y prestaciones. La planta, una de las cuatro explotaciones mineras de Antofagasta en Chile, produjo 240.400 toneladas métricas de cobre el año pasado. Ver más: ¿Cómo el boom del cobre cambia los planes de austeridad de Kast en Chile? Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: Spain's hard left fails to unite before election, hurting chances of staying in power
item.description: Spain's hard-left parties on Saturday presented separate candidate lists for a snap election after talks on a nationwide pact collapsed, reducing Socialist prime minister Pedro Sanchez' chances of staying in power at the head of a leftist coalition.
item.dc:creator: David Latona
item.content:encoded: Spain's hard-left parties on Saturday presented separate candidate lists for a [USN:L8N45R05N TEXT:"snap election"] after talks on a nationwide pact collapsed, reducing Socialist prime minister Pedro Sanchez' chances of staying in power at the head of a leftist coalition. Spain's electoral system disadvantages smaller parties running separately, particularly in less populous provinces, where fewer seats are available. The division could also demoralise left-wing voters, whom organisers hoped to galvanise around [USN:L1N45U0F8 TEXT:"housing protests"] and [USN:L8N3WQ1QB TEXT:"fear of the far right"]. The Broad Front, a platform comprising several parties represented in the minority government, and the other main party on the hard left, Podemos ("We Can"), had been publicly arguing over the leading positions on joint candidate lists for the November 29 election in Madrid and Barcelona, the largest constituencies. Long-standing [USN:L8N3650H2 TEXT:"animosities"] between former comrades-turned-rivals did not help. "These past few days have been very difficult ... some people will be disappointed today, and for that I am sorry," Ada Colau, the former Barcelona mayor and leader of the Broad Front, said at her platform's launch event in Madrid. Podemos, whose lead candidate is former equality minister Irene Montero, had proposed open primaries to determine candidates' positions on joint lists. But the Broad Front refused, arguing there was too little time, and wanted its own preferred candidates to lead the lists in Madrid and Barcelona. Podemos then made a separate pact deal with the Republican Left of Catalonia (ERC), which favours Catalan independence.

item.title: Israeli settlers attack Palestinians, European diplomats in West Bank, Belgium says
item.description: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian civilians, European diplomats and a French mayor in the occupied West Bank on Saturday, Belgium's foreign minister said, a day after settlers beat an American photojournalist.
item.dc:creator: Ali Sawafta, Mohammed Torokman
item.content:encoded: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian civilians, European diplomats and a French mayor in the occupied West Bank on Saturday, Belgium's foreign minister said, a day after settlers beat an [USN:L8N4620II TEXT:"American photojournalist"]. Maxime Prevot said Belgium's consul general to the Palestinians, French and Polish diplomats, and Catholic representatives were among those attacked. A Belgian vehicle was also damaged, he said. "As the occupying power, Israeli authorities must protect Palestinians, ensure the safety of diplomats and journalists, and bring those responsible to justice. Impunity for violent settlers must end," Prevot said in a statement posted on X. 'THROWN TO THE GROUND' Bernard Baudoux, mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries in northern France, told Reuters he had been harvesting olives near the Palestinian Christian village of Taybeh in solidarity with the local community when he was "violently attacked" by masked settlers. "I was thrown to the ground," he said. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar condemned the attack, describing the perpetrators as Israeli rioters. He also suggested the diplomats should have coordinated their visit with the Israeli military. "Such coordination could have helped safeguard the visitors’ security," he said in a statement on X. Palestinian Vice President Hussein al-Sheikh condemned the attack, calling it a small example of the "daily terrorism" to which Palestinians are subjected. Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, have periodically condemned settler violence, while saying it is carried out by a small minority. Palestinians and human rights groups dispute that characterisation. ISRAELI POLICE OPEN INVESTIGATION Settler attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank have surged over the past three years. Journalists, activists and foreign observers have also been targeted. On Friday, dozens of masked settlers attacked Palestinians harvesting olives in the West Bank. Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine, a US citizen covering the harvest, was hospitalised after being assaulted by masked settlers. "Palestinians face this violence every day. Settlers also target journalists reporting on it and diplomats. Harvesting olives, reporting the news or carrying out diplomatic duties should never put anyone at risk of attack," Prevot said. Belgium, which has announced a ban on imports from Israeli settlements in the West Bank and the Golan Heights, will press for European Union sanctions "against those responsible for this violence and those who support them," he added. Polish Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maciej Wewior said on X that a convoy carrying diplomats, including Polish officials, had been attacked. The Polish diplomats were unharmed. "Attacks on members of the diplomatic corps are absolutely unacceptable," he said. Israeli police said they had opened an investigation into the incident. There was no immediate announcement of any arrests. Prosecutions of settlers accused of violent crimes against Palestinians in the West Bank are rare.

item.title: Bayern crush Leipzig 6-1 to live up to coach Kompany's prediction
item.description: Bayern Munich obliterated RB Leipzig 6-1 on Saturday with a scintillating performance, to live up to coach Vincent Kompany's prediction before the game that his team was close to hitting top form.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bayern Munich obliterated RB Leipzig 6-1 on Saturday with a scintillating performance, to live up to coach Vincent Kompany's prediction before the game that his team was close to hitting top form. Kompany had said on Friday his team's consecutive draws in the league and Europe were [USN:L6N4620HY TEXT:"not representative"] of Bayern's current level and his players proved him right, delivering a statement win, with Luis Diaz hitting a hat-trick, to silence critics. The Bavarians had drawn 2-2 against Augsburg while also conceding the [USN:L6N45W03O TEXT:"fastest"] goal in Bundesliga history last week before a shock 3-3 [USN:L6N45Z15P TEXT:"draw"] at outsiders Viking in the Champions League on Tuesday. They had to come from behind in both those matches but against Leipzig it was clear from the start who was boss. Bayern opened their account with Diaz in the 12th minute before the Colombian set up Aleksandar Pavlovic for their second 14 minutes later. Michael Olise, who had terrorised the Leipzig defence in the first half, capped his outstanding performance with a goal in the 34th. Diaz bagged his hat-trick with goals either side of Harry Kane's tap-in on the England captain's 100th Bundesliga appearance. Leipzig scored a late consolation goal in stoppage time. The result lifted the champions into top spot on 14 points, ahead of Borussia Dortmund on goal difference, after the Ruhr valley club slipped up with a goalless draw at Union Berlin. Dortmund, who lost 1-0 in the Champions League at Bodo/Glimt on Wednesday and have now failed to win any of their last three matches across all competitions, lacked spark. They also had striker Konstantinos Karetsas, who had come on in the 62nd minute, go off with an ankle injury just eight minutes later. He had come back after collapsing in September during a Champions League game due to what the club said were 'circulatory problems'. The visitors had to settle for a second consecutive league draw. Freiburg, on 13, are in action against Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday and can reclaim top spot with a win. Werder Bremen became the first Bundesliga team in history to come back from a two-goal deficit in three consecutive league matches when they did it against Paderborn for a 2-2 draw.

item.title: Report: Florida QB Tramell Jones Jr. to start vs. Texas
item.description: Florida quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. will make his first career start on Saturday at No. 7 Texas, ESPN reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Florida quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. will make his first career start on Saturday at No. 7 Texas, ESPN reported. The sophomore takes over for Aaron Philo, who is dealing with a shoulder injury and could be available as an emergency backup when the Gators (4-2, 2-2 SEC) visit the Longhorns (4-1, 1-1) in Austin. Jones replaced Philo in the fourth quarter in last Saturday's 38-19 home loss to South Carolina and threw for 40 yards with one interception. Jones has completed 44 of 64 passes for 443 yards with four touchdowns and two interceptions in seven games over the past two seasons at Florida. --Field Level Media

item.title: Wizards monitoring top overall pick AJ Dybantsa (ankle)
item.description: No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa sustained a mild ankle sprain during the Washington Wizards' preseason finale against the New Orleans Pelicans on Friday, head coach Brian Keefe announced.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa sustained a mild ankle sprain during the Washington Wizards' preseason finale against the New Orleans Pelicans on Friday, head coach Brian Keefe announced. Keefe told sideline reporter Chase Hughes the rookie forward was removed from the game as a precaution and will undergo further testing. "We'll look at it more when we get more information," Keefe said. Dybantsa landed awkwardly and fell to the court following a midrange jumper and limped to the locker room. He scored 12 points in 15 minutes before exiting in the second quarter of the 107-106 setback to New Orleans. The Wizards open the regular season Wednesday against the visiting Milwaukee Bucks. The 6-foot-9 Dybantsa led the nation in scoring at 25.5 points per game during his lone college campaign at BYU. --Field Level Media

item.title: Huracán Trudy se fortalece ligeramente frente a costas del Pacífico mexicano
item.description: El huracán Trudy se fortaleció ligeramente el sábado en aguas del Pacífico mexicano, aunque se espere que se debilite a partir del domingo, mientras avanza hacia el noroeste y se acercaría más tarde a la costa del suroeste y centro de México, afectada por lluvias en las últimas semanas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El huracán Trudy se fortaleció ligeramente el sábado en aguas del Pacífico mexicano, aunque se espere que se debilite a partir del domingo, mientras avanza hacia el noroeste y se acercaría más tarde a la costa del suroeste y centro de México, afectada por lluvias en las últimas semanas. Trudy, categoría 1en la escala de Saffir-Simpson, se ubicaba a 425 kilómetros al oeste del puerto turístico Acapulco, en el estado Guerrero, y soplaba vientos máximos sostenidos de 150 kilómetros por hora (km/h), mientras se movía a 17 km/h, de acuerdo al reporte más reciente del Centro Nacional de Huracanes de Estados Unidos (NHC, por su sigla en inglés). El aviso de huracán estaba vigente para la costa desde el sur de Manzanillo, en el estado Colima, hasta Cabo Corrientes, Jalisco, en el occidente de México. El NHC dijo que se espera que Trudy descargue lluvias de entre 10 a 20 centímetros a lo largo y cerca de la costa de Michoacán, Colima y Jalisco. "Esta lluvia puede producir inundaciones y deslizamientos de tierra que amenazan la vida, especialmente a lo largo de un terreno empinado", señala el reporte. La estatal Comisión Nacional del Agua (Conagua) en México advirtió también que las precipitaciones generadas por Trudy, que llegó a ser un huracán categoría 3, podrían provocar desbordamientos e inundaciones en zonas bajas en las zonas involucradas. En las últimas semanas, la costa del Pacífico mexicano ha sido golpeada por los huracanes[USN:L6N45L0YK TEXT:" Polo"] y[USN:L8N45V0SM TEXT:" Simon,"] y la tormenta Rachel. Debido a las inundaciones, al menos ocho personas perdieron la vida en la ciudad costera de Ensenada, en el estado Baja California.

item.title: Surgen actos de violencia en Francia ante las protestas nacionales de los chalecos amarillos y de los estudiantes
item.description: Los disturbios en Francia no son un caso aislado. Las protestas se están extendiendo por toda Europa, incluyendo España, Italia, Albania y Bélgica, y entre las reivindicaciones de los manifestantes fi ...
item.dc:creator: Samy Adghirni, Francois de Beaupuy
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — La Policía francesa utilizó gas lacrimógeno y procedió a detenciones tras los brotes de violencia registrados en París y otras ciudades antes de las manifestaciones previstas para este sábado en todo el país, convocadas por grupos como el movimiento de los chalecos amarillos. El Ministerio del Interior afirmó que personas a las que describió como agitadores de extrema izquierda encapuchados se reunieron en la capital francesa y en ciudades como Rennes, Toulouse y Angers. Los miembros de estos grupos incendiaron mobiliario urbano y equipamientos, e intentaron saquear comercios, según indicó el ministerio en un comunicado. En Marsella, se saquearon tiendas y se produjeron daños en una comisaría, mientras que en Lyon, las imágenes de televisión mostraban cómo se atacaba e incendiaba una oficina de turismo. Las imágenes también mostraban enfrentamientos entre la Policía y personas que llevaban diversos tipos de sudaderas con capucha, bufandas y máscaras. Según el Ministerio, la policía había detenido a 166 personas en todo el país a mediodía. Durante la noche, un incendio provocado causó daños en un edificio de la Universidad de Ruán, en Normandía. Tras más de tres semanas de disturbios estudiantiles por la financiación de la educación, el Ministerio prevé cientos de “acciones” —como el bloqueo de las cabinas de peaje de las autopistas y de las estaciones de servicio— durante las manifestaciones de este fin de semana. Algunos sindicatos, entre ellos la CGT, también se disponían a sumarse a las protestas, centrándose en cuestiones relacionadas con el gasto público y el poder adquisitivo. “Esperamos una movilización bastante importante” por parte de los manifestantes, declaró el viernes el ministro del Interior, Laurent Núñez, a la cadena France 2. La Policía se estaba preparando para posibles actos violentos por parte de elementos extremistas entre los manifestantes en las ciudades más grandes, añadió. Los disturbios en Francia no son un caso aislado. Las protestas se están extendiendo por toda Europa, incluyendo España, Italia, Albania y Bélgica, y entre las reivindicaciones de los manifestantes figuran viviendas más asequibles y un menor coste de la vida. En Portugal, Tiago Oliveira, líder de la mayor federación sindical del país, la CGTP, afirmó que las manifestaciones que comenzaron el sábado en Lisboa y otras zonas tienen como objetivo dar voz a las personas que se enfrentan al “brutal aumento” de los precios de la vivienda, el combustible y los alimentos. Los chalecos amarillos son un movimiento de base, en ocasiones radical, que surgió en 2018 para luchar contra el aumento del coste de la vida. Sus protestas de aquel año se desencadenaron a raíz de una propuesta de subida del impuesto sobre los combustibles presentada por el presidente Emmanuel Macron. Consideraban que esta medida suponía una carga desproporcionada para los ciudadanos de las zonas rurales y de clase trabajadora que dependen del carro. Aunque el movimiento de masas de los primeros años se disipó en gran medida, los chalecos amarillos nunca han dejado por completo de salir a la calle. La iniciativa del sábado fue propuesta inicialmente por un usuario de TikTok sin una agenda política clara. Los activistas de los chalecos amarillos aprovecharon la oportunidad para intentar reactivar su movimiento con llamamientos en las redes sociales a salir a la calle. Las continuas manifestaciones de los estudiantes de secundaria para protestar por las condiciones de las aulas, las ausencias de los profesores y el acceso a la universidad no guardaban inicialmente relación alguna con los chalecos amarillos. Alrededor del 57% de los franceses apoya el movimiento estudiantil, según una encuesta de Cluster 17 publicada el 11 de octubre. El Gobierno francés se ha comprometido a tener en cuenta las quejas de los estudiantes, pero no está en condiciones de aumentar drásticamente el presupuesto de educación. Mientras se desarrollan los debates en la Asamblea Nacional, el primer ministro Sébastien Lecornu está tratando de obtener el respaldo parlamentario para restringir drásticamente el gasto y reducir el déficit fiscal al 5 % del producto interior bruto en 2027 —el objetivo que no se ha alcanzado este año—. Los grupos de la oposición, que en los últimos dos años han derrocado en dos ocasiones a primeros ministros por sus planes presupuestarios, se muestran reacios a llegar a un acuerdo, a menos de siete meses de las elecciones presidenciales. Las protestas en Portugal se producen tras una manifestación por la vivienda celebrada en Oporto a principios de esta semana, que degeneró en enfrentamientos entre la Policía y los manifestantes acampados en una plaza. Según se ha informado, unas 40 personas resultaron heridas. El primer ministro Luís Montenegro ha rechazado las sugerencias de que los disturbios sean señal de una agitación política más amplia. Los precios de la vivienda en Portugal se dispararon más de un 16 % en el segundo trimestre con respecto al año anterior, el ritmo más rápido de la Unión Europea, según Eurostat. La demanda extranjera y la escasez de viviendas han impulsado este aumento, mientras que la vivienda social representa solo alrededor del 2% del parque inmobiliario del país, una de las proporciones más bajas de la UE. --Con la colaboración de Henrique Almeida. item.title: Kenya confirms four new Ebola cases, bringing total number to seven - Reuters
item.description: Kenya confirms four new Ebola cases, bringing total number to seven Reuters

item.title: Kenya confirms four new Ebola cases, bringing total number to seven
item.description: Kenya confirmed four new cases of the Ebola Bundibugyo virus on Saturday, including three health workers who treated the country's first patient, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to seven, the health ministry said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kenya confirmed four new cases of the Ebola Bundibugyo virus on Saturday, including three health workers who treated the country's first patient, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to seven, the health ministry said. The other new case is a male relative of the index patient, who died. The relative had been in quarantine since October 6, the ministry said in a statement. The cases are the first known infections passed on inside Kenya, where the first patient arrived from Congo on October 3. But the ministry says it has traced and quarantined nearly all of his contacts and there is no evidence that the virus is spreading in the community. The three health workers — two men and a woman aged 29, 35 and 32 respectively — managed the index case on October 3 and 4 and had been in quarantine since October 9, it said. All four new patients were already in quarantine when they developed symptoms and were diagnosed. The second and third patients [USN:L8N4621HW TEXT:"confirmed earlier"] are stable and responding well to supportive treatment, the ministry said. It said 128 of 130 listed contacts, or 98.5%, had been traced and placed in quarantine, higher than the 85% global benchmark it said was needed to break the chain of transmission. Kenya's cases are linked to the Ebola epidemic in Congo — [USN:L8N45Z1AX TEXT:"the second-largest"] outbreak ever recorded, with more than 9,000 cases and more than 4,000 deaths. There are no approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola. The [USN:L8N45S0GY TEXT:"first Kenyan case "]was a man who had been ill in Congo for about a month before travelling by road to Uganda and flying to Nairobi on October 3. He died on October 5. His arrival has raised concerns about screening at the Congo-Uganda border, which has been closed since May, and at Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport. Efforts to trace the remaining two contacts were ongoing, the ministry said. "The risk to the general public remains low as there is no evidence of community transmission," it said, adding that there were no restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings.

item.title: Zelenskiy critica dispensa de sanções à Rússia por Trump como "equivocada"
item.description: A decisão do presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, de conceder uma isenção de sanções e tarifas contra a Rússia poucos dias antes da entrada em vigor levará "infelizmente" a um alívio adicional para Moscou e incentivará novas agressões russas, disse o presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, neste sábado.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh, Jasper Ward
item.content:encoded: A decisão do presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, de conceder uma isenção de sanções e tarifas contra a Rússia poucos dias antes da entrada em vigor levará "infelizmente" a um alívio adicional para Moscou e incentivará novas agressões russas, disse o presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, neste sábado. "A decisão de desfazer tudo isso, de bloquear tudo isso, me parece equivocada", escreveu Zelenskiy na rede social X. "Isso certamente ajuda apenas os russos." Um decreto assinado por Trump na noite de sexta-feira concedeu uma isenção a importantes sanções e tarifas dos EUA relacionadas à Rússia, incluindo tarifas sobre produtos russos e penalidades para a compra de petróleo e gás do país, que estavam programadas para entrar em vigor na próxima semana sob a legislação conhecida como Lei Graham, sancionada por ele no mês passado. Trump afirmou que a isenção atende aos interesses nacionais dos Estados Unidos. A lei tinha como objetivo aumentar a pressão sobre a Rússia por causa da invasão da Ucrânia , que começou em 2022. Trump, no entanto, vem se mostrando mais favorável a Moscou, ao mesmo tempo em que critica publicamente o presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, chegando a sugerir que Kiev precisa de um novo líder. Zelenskiy afirmou que a mais recente medida de Trump fortalece a posição do presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, e incentiva novos ataques da Rússia. "Isso apenas alimenta sua satisfação e seu desejo de continuar matando pessoas", escreveu Zelenskiy, acrescentando que a Rússia atingiu na sexta-feira mais de 15 instalações ucranianas de geração e transmissão de energia. "Isso certamente não põe fim à guerra." O líder ucraniano também acusou a Rússia de planejar intensificar os ataques no oeste da Ucrânia. "A Rússia está se preparando para isso? Eu acredito que sim", escreveu Zelenskiy. Kirill Dmitriev, enviado russo para investimentos, afirmou na sexta-feira que a isenção concedida por Trump representa "um momento verdadeiramente histórico". Em publicação no X, ele disse que, caso as penalidades tivessem entrado em vigor, poderiam ter interrompido de forma efetiva toda a cooperação econômica entre a Rússia e os Estados Unidos. Semanas antes das eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA, nas quais os republicanos de Trump lutam para manter seu estreito controle sobre ambas as câmaras do Congresso, as novas medidas poderiam ter corrido o risco de [USN:L6N45A18J TEXT:"elevar"] ainda mais [USN:L6N45A18J TEXT:"os preços do petróleo"] , enquanto os norte-americanos enfrentam custos crescentes atribuídos em grande parte à guerra dos EUA e de Israel contra o Irã, segundo analistas. A [USN:L6N45A18J TEXT:"legislação,"] cujo principal apoiador no Congresso foi o falecido senador Lindsey Graham, republicano da Carolina do Sul, teria imposto tarifas de até 100% em 30 dias sobre todas as mercadorias trazidas aos EUA dos cinco maiores importadores de petróleo bruto ou gás russo, bem como por qualquer país que, conscientemente, comprasse petróleo ou gás 30 dias após a promulgação da lei ou estivesse entre os cinco principais países que ajudassem a Rússia a contornar as sanções. O decreto diz que a isenção permanecerá em vigor até que Trump ou seus principais assessores determinem que “outras medidas sejam apropriadas”. Trump assinou a Lei Lindsey O. Graham de Sanções à Rússia e ao Irã de 2026 em meados de setembro. “Apresentei ao Congresso uma certificação de que a emissão dessa isenção neste momento é do interesse nacional dos Estados Unidos”, afirmou Trump na ordem. Países como a China e [USN:L1N45G03K TEXT:"a Índia"], que estão entre os maiores compradores de petróleo russo, manifestaram preocupações em relação ao projeto de sanções contra a Rússia. (Reportagem de Kanishka Singh, Jasper Ward e Patricia Zengerle, em Washington; Reportagem adicional de Gleb Bryanski, em Moscou, e Laila Kearney, em Nova York)

item.title: Yes Bank Q2 profit rises but AT1 ruling not booked as further appeal weighed - Reuters
item.description: Yes Bank Q2 profit rises but AT1 ruling not booked as further appeal weighed Reuters

item.title: Yes Bank Q2 profit rises but AT1 ruling not booked as further appeal weighed
item.description: Yes Bank on Saturday reported a 65% jump in second-quarter profit to 10.80 billion Indian rupees ($114 million), but said the figure does not reflect the impact of a Supreme Court ruling this week that set aside its 2020 write-off of 84 billion rupees ($884 million) of additional tier-1 (AT1) bonds.
item.dc:creator: Ashwin Manikandan
item.content:encoded: Yes Bank (YESB.NS) on Saturday reported a 65% jump in second-quarter profit to 10.80 billion Indian rupees ($114 million), but said the figure does not reflect the impact of a Supreme Court ruling this week that set aside its 2020 write-off of 84 billion rupees ($884 million) of additional tier-1 (AT1) bonds. Had the impact been recognised, the bank would have posted a quarterly loss of 52.17 billion rupees, it said in a filing. The Supreme Court on Thursday [USN:L4N4610S4 TEXT:"upheld"] a 2023 Bombay High Court judgment that set aside the write-down, dismissing appeals by the lender, the Reserve Bank of India and the federal government. The Mumbai-based lender, in which Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation [RIC:RIC:SUMFDS.UL] holds a 24.99% stake, said it was evaluating the implications, including the manner and timing of implementation. It is also weighing "all legal remedies available", including further proceedings before the Supreme Court. The figures are indicative and subject to revision, the bank said. If they were adjusted to reflect the court ruling, the bank's net worth would fall to 469.70 billion rupees from 532.68 billion, and borrowings would rise to 861.49 billion rupees from 777.34 billion, it said. Its total capital adequacy ratio would stay unaffected at 14.5%, the bank said. It had said in a filing on Friday that its common equity tier-1 ratio would decline about 250 basis points. AT1 bonds are high-risk debt instruments that can be written off or converted into equity when a bank comes under financial stress. Yes Bank, a mid-sized lender, was rescued in 2020 under a restructuring scheme that brought in new investors. The bonds were written off by an administrator in charge of the restructuring. Analysts had forecast a profit of 9.55 billion rupees, according to LSEG data. The bank's net interest income rose 22.7% to 28.22 billion rupees. Advances grew 23.7% from a year earlier and deposits rose 19.5%. Provisions for bad loans and other contingencies fell 24.2% to 3.17 billion rupees. Other income rose 14.4% to 18.82 billion rupees. The gross non-performing asset ratio was 1.2% at end-September, against 1.3% at end-June. ($1 = 94.9600 Indian rupees)

item.title: High debt, growing strains put focus on need for new development approaches
item.description: High debt levels, rising debt-service costs and a sharp drop in official development assistance are forcing developing countries and institutions that help them to rethink development and look for new sources of funding, including from the private sector.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal, Rae Wee
item.content:encoded: High debt levels, rising debt-service costs and a sharp drop in official development assistance are forcing developing countries and institutions that help them to rethink development and look for new sources of funding, including from the private sector. World Bank President Ajay Banga, who has led a drive that has more than tripled the [USN:L1N4580ZW TEXT:"private capital"] flowing to development projects since 2022, told the annual IMF and World Bank meetings that changes were needed to help countries address headwinds posed by persistent conflicts, a drop in official development assistance and rising debt burdens. A huge demographic challenge was also unfolding, he said, with some 1.2 billion young people likely to join the job market in the next 10 to 15 years, but only 400 million jobs in sight. The answer, Banga said, would depend on bringing public finance, private investment, philanthropy and technology together to meet each country's needs. British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said he would make [USN:L1N4600EL TEXT:"debt restructuring"] and other help for the poorest countries a key theme for Britain's upcoming G20 presidency. But he said the private sector needed to step up since Britain and other rich nations could not provide the same level of support as during the last big debt forgiveness push at the turn of the millennium. "The risks of lending to emerging markets have been overestimated and the risk of default has been overestimated," he told a panel on Wednesday hosted by the Rockefeller Foundation, a private US foundation that works on development. Developing countries are also looking for answers outside the two Bretton Woods institutions, disappointed by the response to high debt levels, climate change, worsening inequality and geopolitical challenges. "The world has, in many ways, changed for the worse since 2023," Shekhar Aiyar, director and chief executive of the Indian Council for Research on International Economic Relations, told an event hosted by the Center for Global Development this week. "Developing countries have been caught in a downward spiral of decelerating growth and increased vulnerability ... at the same time, there has been a vast scaling back of bilateral aid." International aid from OECD Development Assistance Committee donor countries fell 23% in real terms in 2025, marking the biggest annual drop in the history of ODA. The top five donors — the US, Germany, UK, Japan and France — all cut aid, together accounting for 96% of the total drop. Meanwhile, according to UNCTAD — the official UN body responsible for trade, investment and development issues — developing countries' combined external debt stock reached $12.3 trillion in the same year, up by half a trillion from 2024. NEW PARTNERSHIPS AND APPROACHES US President Donald Trump's sweeping tariffs have added to strains and prompted many developing countries and emerging markets to forge new trade partnerships that do not include the United States. Indian Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman told an Atlantic Council broadcast that countries like hers were plowing ahead with more bilateral partnerships. "I feel this approach of 'Yes, we want multilateralism, but yet we're not waiting for it, we are going ahead with bilateral,' has really rewarded India," Sitharaman said. Eric LeCompte, executive director of Jubilee USA Network, which advocates for debt relief, said this year's meetings were a big disappointment for developing countries, providing no new initiative to help those already facing steep debt-service payments and now saddled with soaring borrowing costs. He said the IMF failed to reach critical mass to launch its expanded Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust, which lends to low-income countries at low interest rates, and barely mentioned its Catastrophe Containment and Relief Trust, which provides grants for debt relief to the world's poorest countries. "There was a lot of information about how challenging problems are, but we saw hardly any action," he said, aside from tweaks to debt restructuring plans by the Global Sovereign Debt Roundtable. "We were expecting more," he said. Jean Saldanha, director of the European Network on Debt and Development, asked: "Where are the emergency measures to stop countries in the Global South being forced to spend more on debt than on health and education? And where are the serious policy responses to the escalating climate emergency, boosted by a Super El Niño?" "The least-developed countries have said loud and clear they need more climate grants, less debt, simpler access and faster disbursements," she said. Muhammad Al Jasser, who chairs the Islamic Development Bank group, told Reuters there was growing interest in securing private sector funds to augment increasingly scarce public resources. "The challenges are huge. We're not going to solve them either single-handedly or even collectively in a short period of time, but I think we are (heading) in the right direction," he said, adding his bank was aiming to deploy $10 billion in financing next year.

item.title: Australia still undecided on starting XI for second test v S Africa
item.description: Australia are assessing all selection options ahead of the second test against South Africa in Gqeberha on Sunday as they look to claim the three-match test series following a thumping 214-run win in the opening game.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia are assessing all selection options ahead of the second test against South Africa in Gqeberha on Sunday as they look to claim the three-match test series following a thumping 214-run win in the opening game. All-rounder Cameron Green will miss out again with an abdominal strain but wicketkeeper-batter Josh Inglis could win his race to recover from a finger injury. Whether he would start if fit remains to be seen, as Australia also ponder an all seam bowling attack that would leave out experienced spinner Nathan Lyon. With bad weather expected on the first two days there is a chance that the game could be shortened, or that conditions would be heavily weighted in favour of the seamers. "We always look at all options," captain Pat Cummins told reporters on Saturday. "We love playing with Nath. We saw last week, (he took) a couple of key wickets in the first innings. And even the control he gives. It makes the rest of us fast bowlers be able to function around him." He suggested that Matt Renshaw, who scored 190 and 82 in the first test in Durban, would remain as a middle order batter, rather than an option to open the innings as he has done before. "After what Renners did last week, I presume he'll stay at number five," Cummins said. "What he deserved even more credit for is that we'd asked him to do a different role and he just said straight away 'yep, no worries, whatever the team needs'. "There were so many positives in addition to the runs he scored last week. He was a delight, and really helped me and Lyon get through those partnerships (with Renshaw)." South Africa lead the head-to-head in Gqeberha 4-3, with Australia’s last victory there coming in 1997.

item.title: Egypt's Sisi seeks parliament's backing to help defend Saudi Arabia if asked
item.description: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Saturday Egypt would take any measures necessary to defend Saudi Arabia if asked, amid escalating Houthi attacks on the kingdom, and parliament announced an emergency session on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Saturday Egypt would take any measures necessary to defend Saudi Arabia if asked, amid escalating Houthi attacks on the kingdom, and parliament announced an emergency session on Sunday. "It is inconceivable that we would allow Saudi Arabia, its security or stability to be harmed," Sisi said at a graduation ceremony at the Egyptian Military Academy. He said Egypt was not seeking to attack anyone, but was prepared to act in defence. Yemen's Iran-aligned [USN:L1N45Z0HH TEXT:"Houthis"] have in recent days attacked [USN:L1N45W03M TEXT:"Riyadh's international airport"] and the state oil giant [USN:L1N45Z0HH TEXT:"Saudi Aramco"], amid renewed fighting with the Saudi-backed forces of the internationally recognised government following the collapse of a truce. Sisi said Egypt would act in accordance with guidance from Saudi King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, who [USN:S8N452004 TEXT:"visited Sisi"] on September 15, after fighting in Yemen reignited, to discuss issues including security and navigation in the Red Sea. "I know this requires the approval of the Egyptian parliament, and I ask that an emergency session be held so that it can give us that authorisation if we are asked," Sisi said. Shortly after he spoke, parliament said it would hold a plenary session at 1 p.m. (1000 GMT) on Sunday in response to the request, though it did not disclose the agenda. Egypt and Saudi Arabia are close strategic and economic partners. Saudi Arabia and other oil-rich Gulf states provided Egypt with billions of dollars in aid, central-bank deposits and investments after the military ouster of Islamist president Mohamed Morsi in 2013. Egypt also joined the Saudi-led coalition that intervened in 2015 to support the Yemeni government against the Houthis.

item.title: Protesters clash with police in Brussels
item.description: Police used tear gas and water cannon, while some protesters overturned a car.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Several hundred mostly young people protested in Brussels on Saturday, with rioters clashing with police in unrest partly inspired by demonstrations in [USN:L1N46302B TEXT:"neighbouring France"]. Belgian student groups have said they are protesting against rising education costs and reforms they fear will make higher education less accessible. Demonstrators gathered in central Brussels, many wearing masks and chanting anti-fascist slogans. Police used tear gas and water cannon, while some protesters overturned a car, according to a Reuters witness. Belgian Interior Minister Bernard Quintin said in a post on X that "what is unfolding in Brussels is no longer mere protest" and "all necessary means will be used to restore order in the face of the rioters". A protest also took place in the eastern city of Liège, where students earlier this month demonstrated over the French-language education system, citing rising education costs and difficulties accessing study materials. The unrest in France began last month as protests over education funding and school conditions before broadening into a wider movement centred on inequality, public spending and living standards.

item.title: Injured Swiatek goes down fighting in Wuhan Open semi-final
item.description: A left-leg injury derailed Iga Swiatek.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A left-leg injury derailed Iga Swiatek as she went down fighting to Polish compatriot and childhood friend Maja Chwalinska 7-5 6-1 in the Wuhan Open semi-finals on Saturday. French Open runner-up Chwalinska, who was Swiatek's junior doubles partner, will face Sonay Kartal in the final after the Briton beat Jelena Ostapenko 7-6(9) 7-6(5) in the first semi-final. Swiatek was 5-3 ahead in the first set but fellow 25-year-old Chwalinska saved two set points and took a 6-5 lead before the six-time Grand Slam winner had to take a medical timeout. After receiving treatment, Swiatek continued the match with a bandaged left thigh, but found it difficult to put pressure on her leg and struggled to chase returns across the court. She completed the match and the two players, who have known each other since they were 10, shared a quiet handshake after their first competitive clash in 10 years. Swiatek's physio Maciej Ryszczuk posted on X: "I told her three times to stop the match because it was a risk to her health. "She made the decision herself to carry on playing, and since she’s made that decision, I’ll support her as best I can." An emotional Chwalinska said she could not believe she had won. "She is a great champion, living legend, she won everything. So it was a great honour for me to share the court with her today," Chwalinska said about Swiatek. With Swiatek losing, world number six Elina Svitolina secured her place in the WTA Finals, becoming the seventh player to qualify for next month's year-ending championship, with only one spot still up for grabs. KARTAL BEATS ERROR-PRONE OSTAPENKO Former French Open champion Ostapenko was left ruing her mistakes as she squandered 4-1 leads in both sets to lose to Kartal, who is ranked 136 places below the Latvian. Ostapenko was undone by her 41 unforced errors, including two straight double faults while serving for the first set. She hit the ground with her racket, frustrated with wayward and netted returns, as Kartal stayed calm to reach her second final on the tour. "At times she is unplayable and sometimes you just have to ride the wave. Mentally, I think this is one of the best performances I've had in my career," said the 24-year-old Kartal, who returned in September after a six-month absence due to a back injury. Both Kartal and Chwalinska will play their first WTA 1000 final when they face each other on Sunday.

item.title: Hurricane Trudy threatens western Mexico with heavy rain, coastal flooding
item.description: Hurricane Trudy maintained its strength as it moved toward Mexico's western coast on Saturday, with forecasters warning it could strengthen further before beginning to weaken on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hurricane Trudy maintained its strength as it moved toward Mexico's western coast on Saturday, with forecasters warning it could strengthen further before beginning to weaken on Sunday. The US National Hurricane Center said Trudy was about 190 miles (305 km) south-southeast of Manzanillo early on Saturday, with maximum sustained winds of 90 mph (150 kph). The hurricane was moving at about 8 mph (13 kph) and was forecast to approach southwestern and west-central Mexico later on Saturday before passing near the coast overnight into Sunday. Hurricane conditions are expected in the warning area on Saturday night, while tropical storm conditions are expected to spread across the region during the day, the NHC said. Hurricane conditions are also possible in areas under a hurricane watch. Trudy is forecast to bring four to eight inches (10 to 20 cm) of rain, with isolated totals of around 15 inches, across parts of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco through the weekend, raising the risk of life-threatening flooding and landslides, especially in steep terrain, according to the NHC. Outer rain bands could produce two to four inches of rain, with isolated totals of around six inches, in Guerrero and Nayarit, where localized flash flooding is possible, the center said. The NHC also warned of possible coastal flooding from storm surge in areas exposed to onshore winds, accompanied by large and destructive waves. Swells generated by Trudy were already affecting parts of Mexico's southwestern coast and are expected to spread northward toward the country's west-central coast through the weekend, creating life-threatening surf and rip current conditions, the NHC said.

item.title: Bank of Canada sees sharply higher inflation outlook as oil surges, Macklem says
item.description: The Bank of Canada expects to raise its quarterly inflation forecast significantly this month owing to persistently high crude oil and petroleum product prices, Governor Tiff Macklem said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Promit Mukherjee
item.content:encoded: The Bank of Canada expects to raise its quarterly inflation forecast significantly this month owing to persistently high crude oil and petroleum product prices, Governor Tiff Macklem said on Saturday. New quarterly inflation and growth forecasts will feed into the BoC's rate decision on October 28. "With the (Middle East) conflict ongoing, shipments still curtailed and refinery capacity damage, the risk that inflation broadens and becomes more persistent has gone up," Macklem told journalists on a conference call from Bangkok. "Our beacon is our 2% inflation target, and we are committed to keeping inflation close to target over time. We are prepared to adjust monetary policy as needed." Money market expectations of an increase in rates have been growing in the last few months but, as of Saturday, markets were not pricing in any change on October 28 or at the bank's last monetary policy decision of the year in December. However, they are pricing in increases of 100 basis points over the course of next year. Macklem said the global economy had shown resilience despite the conflict in the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine war, but that resilience was being tested by higher costs and tighter financial conditions. He said governments also had less fiscal room to maneuver and needed to adjust their policies to rebuild that capacity. For central bankers, the main concern is to ascertain whether higher oil and product prices will spill over into the broader economy. Speaking about the decision to be made on October 28, Macklem said: "The question we are going to be asking ourselves is, 'Is inflation likely to come back down towards our target on its own, or are we going to have to raise interest rates to influence the path, nudge the path for inflation back towards the target?'."

item.title: Haaland double helps Man City win, Neto brace cheers Chelsea
item.description: Argentina international Emi Martinez was taken to hospital following a clash of heads with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite.
item.dc:creator: Martyn Herman
item.content:encoded: Manchester City bounced back from their midweek setback in Europe to maintain their perfect Premier League start with Erling Haaland's double propelling them to a 3-2 home win over battling Ipswich Town on Saturday. Paris St Germain inflicted a first meaningful defeat on Enzo Maresca's side in the Champions League on Wednesday but City shrugged off a gallant Ipswich side to make it seven wins from seven to cement their place at the top of the table. Chelsea beat Everton 2-0 in Saturday's early action thanks to Pedro Neto's brace although the London club's win was overshadowed by an injury to [USN:L4N46302T TEXT:"goalkeeper Emi Martinez"]. Liverpool came from a goal down to beat Brentford 2-1 away although they were helped by the previously unbeaten hosts being reduced to 10 men shortly before halftime when Yehor Yarmolyuk was shown a straight red card for a head butt. Manchester City have 21 points, six ahead of second-placed champions Arsenal, who visit Nottingham Forest on Sunday. Liverpool's win lifted them above Brentford into fifth place with 12 points behind Chelsea in fourth on 13. Third-placed Brighton & Hove Albion, who also have 13 points, host Crystal Palace on Sunday. Fulham moved off the foot of the table with their first league win of the season -- 1-0 at home to Hull City -- while Aston Villa won by the same scoreline at Newcastle United. BUSINESS AS USUAL FOR CITY Dark clouds remain over the Etihad Stadium with Manchester City's fate still unknown after they appealed a ruling that the club breached 114 Premier League financial rules. City have always denied any wrongdoing. But on the pitch it is very much business as usual, especially for Norwegian goal machine Haaland. Phil Foden gave City a short-lived lead cancelled out by Daizen Maeda, but Haaland restored the home side's advantage before halftime with a header from Mateo Kovacic's cross. Haaland then gave his side some breathing space with his second in the 69th minute, powering past Ipswich's Abdoul Ouattara before a low finish into the corner. He was denied a hat-trick by an offside decision and Ipswich got a lifeline when Zian Flemming tucked away a penalty in stoppage time but City bagged the points. The defiant mood was soured somewhat though as [USN:L8N46309A TEXT:"Haaland went off"] with an apparent injury late on, as did Mateo Kovacic, Matheus Nunes and Nico O'Reilly, while Antoine Semenyo was also limping badly at the final whistle. "I don't know (Haaland's injury)," Maresca said. "I asked him. He said that he was okay. So hopefully, it's nothing serious." FEISTY FIRST HALF Chelsea have had a knack of scoring early this season but were kept at bay by hosts Everton in a feisty and physical first half that produced five yellow cards. However, Xabi Alonso's visitors needed just 43 seconds after the restart to go 1-0 up when Jorrel Hato cut the ball back from the byline to find Neto who swept home. Keeper Martinez's clash of heads with Jarrad Branthwaite resulted in the Argentine being strapped to a stretcher and taken off, leading to 11 minutes of stoppage time. Chelsea doubled their lead in the 90th minute when Neto pounced on a loose ball after Jordan Henderson's free kick was blocked by the wall, finding the bottom corner with a composed finish as Everton suffered their first defeat of the season. "What we know is he (Martinez) left the stadium conscious and right now he is in the hospital doing precautionary tests," Alonso said. "It was concussion but more than that I saw only one clip. Hopefully it won't be too bad but we need to wait." Martinez's knock gave 21-year-old keeper Mike Penders the chance to make his Premier League debut and he helped Chelsea keep a clean sheet in the league for the first time in 23 games. "We need a clean sheet, to be honest. I think we did a very good game. Emi deserved this, Mike did as well," Alonso added. BRENTFORD'S YARMOLYUK SENT OFF Liverpool deservedly fell behind at Brentford with Keane Lewis-Potter putting the hosts in front. Brentford were good value for their lead but Yarmolyuk's rush of blood to the head when he clashed with Jeremy Jacquet at a Liverpool corner changed the game. After referee John Brooks was invited to check a VAR monitor he brandished the red card at Ukrainian Yarmolyuk. Liverpool huffed and puffed after the break but Victor Munoz finally levelled in the 62nd minute when he cut in to beat keeper Caoimhin Kelleher with a left-foot finish. Alexander Isak won it for Andoni Iraola's side eight minutes later with a clinical strike from Bradley Barcola's assist. Brentford ended with nine men after Vitaly Janelt got a second yellow card for a foul on substitute Rio Ngumoha. Alex Iwobi's 33rd-minute strike for Fulham was enough to earn their new manager Alvaro Arbeloa a long-overdue league win and move Fulham up to 16th. Johan Manzambi's early goal secured Villa's victory at Newcastle, their second of the season.

The fire broke out at a three-storey wooden resort The resort was operating without a valid fire safety licence, fire service officials said A five-member investigation committee has been formed to investigate the cause of the fire Authorities also said they would examine possible regulatory failures The incident has raised concerns about fire safety compliance at tourist resorts in the coastal district

item.title: Iran's Guards say two tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said on Saturday that two oil tankers had caught fire after hitting naval mines while crossing the Strait of Hormuz, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said on Saturday that two oil tankers had caught fire after hitting naval mines while crossing the Strait of Hormuz, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported. State media said both tankers were carrying about 2 million barrels of crude oil. There was no independent confirmation of the reports. IRNA reported that the vessels had switched off their positioning and radar systems and attempted to use an unauthorised route through the strategic waterway. The second vessel was left immobilised after striking a mine, it added. State media earlier reported that the other tanker had also struck a mine while attempting to transit the strait via a route not authorised by Iran. The incidents come amid heightened tensions around the strait, a key oil shipping route. Disruptions to shipping in the waterway due to the US-Israeli war on Iran have boosted global energy prices and inflation. Maritime officials said on Wednesday that a container ship and a dry bulk carrier [USN:L1N4600JW TEXT:"sank"] near the strait after being hit by projectiles in separate incidents. [USN:L1N45U0E0 TEXT:"Attacks"] around the waterway have surged over the past two weeks, with Iran saying it is stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions imposed last month.

item.title: Zelenskiy asked neighbours to let grain cargoes through, Hungary PM Magyar says
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy has asked neighbours Poland, Romania, Slovakia and Hungary to allow the transit of Ukrainian grain cargoes because of a Black Sea blockade, Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy has asked neighbours Poland, Romania, Slovakia and Hungary to allow the transit of Ukrainian grain cargoes because of a Black Sea blockade, Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar said on Saturday. Magyar, who agreed with Zelenskiy to [USN:L8N4620U6 TEXT:"reset Ukraine-Hungary ties"] at talks on Friday, said he would have no objections to the measure if the Ukrainian grain cargoes only passed through Hungary to other destinations, private broadcaster RTL reported. Ukraine is among the world's top producers of wheat, corn and sunflower seeds and around 90% of its exports of such crops go through the Black Sea, where a Russian campaign of attacks has [USN:L8N44605L TEXT:"almost halted agricultural exports"] from its Black Sea ports. The grain transit would be modelled on a solution proposed shortly after Russia's February 2022 invasion of Ukraine , Magyar said. "(Zelenskiy) asked Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Hungary and all neighbouring countries to allow transit, as they had three or four years ago at the start of the war," Magyar told RTL in an interview. Magyar has taken a less confrontational stance towards Kyiv than Viktor Orban, whom he succeeded as Hungary's prime minister. Magyar had repeatedly said, however, that Hungary would not send arms to Ukraine and demanded progress on the rights of its ethnic Hungarian minority. Magyar also assured Zelenskiy of his full solidarity over the "inhuman Russian aggression" against Ukraine. "He mentioned to me during our one-on-one meeting that it would help them a lot if they could transport maize in sealed trains to Western Europe," Magyar said. "I said as long as it merely transits the country, there would be no obstacle." In late August the European Commission forecast the European Union's maize harvest, typically its second-largest cereals crop, would be 50.1 million metric tons this year, a near two-decade low and about a fifth below the average of the past three years. Farmers in France and Hungary were hit especially hard as record heat and drought had [USN:L8N44T097 TEXT:"decimated maize plantings"].

item.title: China central bank chief supports closer IMF surveillance of fiscal, spillover risks
item.description: China's central bank governor said on Saturday that Beijing supports the International Monetary Fund in boosting the surveillance of fiscal risks in "major advanced economies" and their spillover effects.
item.dc:creator: Selena Li
item.content:encoded: China's central bank governor said on Saturday that Beijing supports the International Monetary Fund in boosting the surveillance of fiscal risks in "major advanced economies" and their spillover effects. People's Bank of China Governor Pan Gongsheng was addressing the International Monetary and Financial Committee meeting during annual gatherings of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok. Surging borrowing costs, chronic high fiscal deficits in major economies, and turbulent investor sentiment, aggravated by massive capital expenditures in artificial intelligence, have triggered a widespread global [USN:L1N45N05N TEXT:"bond market rout"]. Pan urged the IMF to analyse global imbalances and place greater emphasis on the impact of financial factors such as capital flows on these imbalances, a statement from the bank showed. The central bank chief said China supports the multilateral trading system and opposes all forms of protectionist measures. Earlier this week, IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said China [USN:S0N40K04E TEXT:"must pivot"] from export-led growth towards more domestic consumption.

item.title: Zelenskiy hopes for meeting with US and Russia during G20 summit
item.description: Ukraine, the United States and Russia could meet during a G20 summit in the US but Washington and Moscow have not confirmed the meeting and other venues are also possible, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukraine, the United States and Russia could meet during a G20 summit in the US but Washington and Moscow have not confirmed the meeting and other venues are also possible, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Saturday. The Group of 20 major economies, which includes the US and Russia but not Ukraine, is due to hold a summit in Miami in December. "The meeting could then take place in the United States during the G20 summit. But there has been no confirmation yet from either Russia or the United States. It could also be held in a European country," Zelenskiy told reporters in a WhatsApp media chat. He added: "This meeting could take place in one of the Middle Eastern countries. The United States has consistently mentioned the United Arab Emirates or Saudi Arabia." Zelenskiy said Ukrainian negotiators had spoken to US officials on Friday but gave no other details. He also said that Europe needed its own track for talks with Russia, with which relations are strained by Moscow's war in Ukraine . US President Donald Trump has [USN:L1N463009 TEXT:"declined"] to impose tougher sanctions on Russia over the more than four-year-old war, and Zelenskiy has [USN:L1N4620UE TEXT:"criticised"] Trump for lifting sanctions on Russian diesel exports. STARLINK Zelenskiy said the Ukrainian military was unable to use its interceptors against Russian drone attacks because of speed restrictions placed on services provided by satellite company Starlink. "Today, our interceptor drones are not operating because of speed limitations," Zelenskiy said. He said Ukraine had been told that the speed restrictions had been caused by technical issues but that tests of Starlink on the territory of the European Union had shown there were no such issues there. Trump [USN:L6N462112 TEXT:"said"] on Friday he did not think either he or Elon Musk - whose company SpaceX developed the Starshield system used by Ukraine's military - was responsible for Ukraine losing Starlink access in a way that affected its military operations against Russia. The reduction in services provided by the satellite company [USN:L8N46213X TEXT:"interrupted communications"] with headquarters and caused internet speeds to drop.
