item.title: トランプ氏、対ロシア制裁法の適用を発動直前に免除
item.description:
Kanishka Singh Jasper Ward
[ワシントン １６日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Kanishka Singh　Jasper Ward

[ワシントン １６日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は先月署名した法律に基づくロシア関連の主要な制裁と関税の適用を免除した。ロシア製品への関税や、同国の石油・天然ガスを購入する国への制裁が対象となる。これらは数日後に発効する予定だった。

ホワイトハウスが１６日に公表した大統領令で、トランプ氏は適用免除が米国の国益にかなうと説明した。免除はトランプ氏または政府高官が「追加措置が適切」と判断するまで有効となる。

同法は共和党の故リンゼー・グラム上院議員が推進し、トランプ氏が９月中旬に署名した。ロシア産原油・天然ガスの輸入上位５カ国から米国に輸入される製品に、３０日以内に最大１００％の関税を課す内容となっていた。法律成立から３０日後以降にロシア産と知りながら石油・天然ガスを購入した国や、ロシアの制裁逃れを支援する上位５カ国も対象に含まれていた。

トランプ氏は大統領令で「現時点でこうした適用免除を行うことが米国の国益にかなうとする証明書を議会に提出した」と述べた。同法では、大統領は制裁が国益にかなわないと判断したと議会に通知するだけで、制裁を免除できる。

バージニア州選出のドン・ベイヤー民主党下院議員は、今回の措置を強く批判した。声明で「トランプ氏は今回もプーチン（ロシア大統領）に屈し、パートナーであるウクライナを再び裏切った。ロシアの違法な侵略戦争を罰するための法律に込められた議会の明確な意思にも背いている」と述べた。

トランプ氏は最近ロシアと結んだ軽油に関する合意でも、一部の共和党議員を含む複数の米上院議員から批判を受けていた。

item.title: IMFC chair says global economy resilient; delegates walk out on Russian official
item.description: A US official said Washington supports Russia's presence despite European concerns.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal, David Lawder, Jan Strupczewski
item.content:encoded: The global economy is showing great resilience but there is no room for complacency, the head of the International Monetary Fund's steering committee said on Saturday, while divisions over Russia's war against Ukraine sparked a walkout of delegates. Saudi Finance Minister Mohammed Al-Jadaan, who heads the IMF's steering committee, asked about the walkout by nearly half of delegates during remarks by Russia's finance minister at a meeting on Saturday, said the important thing was that members ultimately agreed to the chair's statement. "We came here for a reason, and we achieved it. Look at this chair statement, it clearly says that all members agreed to the statement, so that's what matters," the chair of the International Monetary and Financial Committee told Reuters. Al-Jadaan told a press conference that the global economy was demonstrating "[USN:L1N463024 TEXT:"remarkable resilience"]" in the face of profound ongoing challenges, including wars, threats to energy and food security, high public debt levels, and risks linked to the rapid development of artificial intelligence, while warning finance officials against letting down their guard. "The message from the IMFC members is clear: There is no room for complacency," Al-Jadaan said in the final press conference of a week of IMF and World Bank annual meetings that brought more than 18,000 people to Bangkok. Fiscal authorities should work to rebuild buffers while protecting vulnerable populations and growth-enhancing investments, Al-Jadaan told reporters, underscoring the need for continued central bank independence and policies that supported private sector-led growth and investment. He said IMFC members called for increasing support to countries that are facing short-term financing challenges caused by spillovers from wars and high energy prices. "International cooperation remains critical to addressing excessive global imbalances and trade tensions," he said. IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva called the meetings productive but said there was clearly heightened anxiety among members about increasing divergence. Many lower income countries that were not part of the AI-value chain feared they were falling behind, she said. "These meetings also have shown that in a world of repetitive shocks and geopolitical fragmentation, still there is desire for multilateral dialogue and cooperation," she said. The Development Committee, which groups the boards of both the World Bank and the IMF, touched on similar themes in its statement, underscoring the urgent need to end wars and conflicts to ensure sustainable growth and long-term stability. "Our priority remains to promote macroeconomic and financial stability while enabling broad-based, private sector-led growth, and strengthening resilience through credible policies and international cooperation," the committee's chair, Swedish Finance Minister Elisabeth Svantesson, said. WALKOUT AMID TENSIONS Those comments came shortly after many IMFC delegates left the room when Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov addressed the group in Russian. Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel told a bank event on the sidelines of the meetings that nearly 50% of delegates took part in the walkout, sending a clear message to Russia. "This is a very strong signal about solidarity and values. It would be the best for the world economy if this unprovoked war of aggression against Ukraine would end," Nagel said. "I was really proud so many left this plenary." Ukraine's central bank chief, Andriy Pyshnyi, told Reuters he was surprised by the large number of finance officials who left the room, calling it a [USN:L1N46303F TEXT:""deep and emotional moment.""] The Bank of England confirmed that Governor Andrew Bailey was among the delegates who joined the walkout, which comes ahead of Britain hosting the G20 next year. European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde, who may be in the frame to take over as [USN:L6N4610XU TEXT:"chair of the World Economic Forum"], stayed in the room, two people in the meeting said. Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 has roiled the IMFC, preventing it from reaching consensus statements in the years since. There were deep divisions again this week as [USN:L1N46209U TEXT:"tensions flared between the US and Ukraine"]. People in the meeting said those who left while Siluanov spoke included delegates from Britain, Germany, France, Denmark, Sweden, Finland, Norway, Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia, among others. "The Ukraine war is existential for us in Europe," one European diplomat said. "We cannot normalize relations with Russia." Germany on Thursday warned against efforts to [USN:L1N4610HQ TEXT:"bring Russia back"] on to the international stage after Siluanov attended a meeting of G20 finance ministers and central bankers, just over a month after the US hosted his first in-person G20 appearance since Russia invaded Ukraine, at a meeting in Asheville, North Carolina. US Treasury Under Secretary Erin Browne told Reuters the same day that Washington, the current leader of the G20, supported Russia's presence. "We think it's really important if you're going to solve a crisis, you need to have open dialogue and open conversation," she told Reuters. "And you can't have ... dialogue, and you can't have resolution to conflict if no one's talking to one another." Ukraine's finance minister participated virtually in the meetings, in order to focus on budget priorities at home. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, speaking at a European Union summit on Friday, blasted US President Donald Trump's recent [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"diesel deal"] with Russia. EU leaders have rallied around Zelenskiy after Trump again criticised Ukraine and called its strikes on Russian refineries a "disgrace." Trump on Friday [USN:L1N463009 TEXT:"waived"] a new congressional requirement to impose harsh sanctions on Russia.

item.title: Mass protests in France spiral into worst riots in years
item.description: Authorities reported violent incidents in several cities, including vandalism in Marseille and attacks targeting police, media and public buildings.
item.dc:creator: Janis Laizans, Stamos Prousalis , Yann Tessier
item.content:encoded: Rioting erupted in cities across France on Saturday as demonstrations against rising living costs and declining public services spiralled out of control in some of the worst violence the country has witnessed for decades. While hundreds of thousands protested peacefully in street marches in scores of cities, violent fringe groups targeted public buildings, looted luxury boutiques and supermarkets and attacked police vehicles and officers. In Limoges the city hall was set ablaze, in Marseille black-clad protesters broke into City Hall and defaced the building with anarchic graffiti and in Lyon protesters torched the city's tourist office. French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said the government would not be "intimidated" by violence, and blamed the unrest on the "far-left" and criminals just months before a presidential election next year. "To those who clearly want to use this violence as a 'warm-up' before the presidential election, I say clearly: We will not let ourselves be intimidated. No one will impose their political agenda through violence," he wrote in a post on X. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez told reporters that about 400 people had been arrested after violent incidents, most of whom were adults. Around 550,000 people had participated in the demonstrations across the country, he said. The CGT union told Reuters it estimated protesters at 800,000 people. President Emmanuel Macron vowed to prosecute and punish people who had performed such attacks. "We will all stand united against the sowers of chaos, who only seek to undermine our institutions and prevent those who peacefully express their demands from doing so," he wrote in a post on X. Belgium, Portugal and Italy also faced smaller-scale protests on Saturday as living costs rise in Europe, while protesters in Albania again rallied against perceived government corruption, a lack of jobs and poor education standards. Protesters said most people had marched peacefully, and put much of the violence down to troublemakers who had set out to cause damage and clash with the police. Many held signs bearing slogans against the police, the president and the wealthy. "We are fighting because the cost of living is too harsh, because the price of fuel is too high, because high school pupils are being violently attacked and hurt all over the country just for trying to protest and ask for more teachers and decent learning conditions," said Lola, a 19-year-old protester in Paris. TEAR GAS, FIRE AND LOOTING Most protests kicked off around midday, with some beginning before the official start of the demonstrations. In some parts of Paris, police fired tear gas rounds as they retreated in the face of mostly young protesters, many of whom were dressed in black and wore hoodies, masks and goggles to protect against tear gas. Rioters tried to break into the Galeries Lafayette department store, smashed up banks, ransacked a Lacoste store as well as other boutiques and looted an SFR mobile phone shop. Protesters had been setting objects ablaze all day, including numerous cars. In protests partly inspired by those in France, several hundred mostly young people protested in [USN:L6N46303L TEXT:"Brussels"], and some clashed with police. Belgian student groups have said they are protesting against rising education costs and reforms they fear will make higher education less accessible. In [USN:L6N46303U TEXT:"Albania"], police fired what appeared to be rubber bullets at protesters during a fifth day of mass student demonstrations calling for Prime Minister Edi Rama to step down. In [USN:L8N46304H TEXT:"Portugal"], tens of thousands took to the streets of Lisbon following days of unrest to protest against housing and other living costs. Housing prices in Portugal have doubled since 2017, fuelling one of the worst affordability crises in Europe. In Italy, a march against high costs of living in [USN:L8N463090 TEXT:"Milan"] degenerated into disorder, with police clearing the central cathedral square with tear gas. Police in Bologna used water cannons to try to disperse crowds and made seven arrests after another protest turned violent, the ANSA news agency reported. FRENCH POLICE RESPONSE UNDER SCRUTINY The protests in France began last month at high schools in Paris' working-class northern suburbs, where anger over teacher shortages and shabby facilities evolved into a broader movement focused on inequality, public spending and living standards. In Paris on Saturday, protesters in high-visibility vests blocked streets, recalling the Yellow Vest movement that marked President Emmanuel Macron's previous term in office. Saturday's protests eclipsed the size of the crowds at the peak of the Yellow Vest movement, though they were far lower than the levels seen at the protests in 2023 against Macron's pension overhaul. Macron is entering [USN:L1N45Y033 TEXT:"the final stretch"] of his presidency, facing a fragmented political landscape and growing pressure over the economy. France's efforts to reduce public debt have failed to reassure investors, pushing government [USN:L8N45R0RA TEXT:"borrowing costs"] to their highest levels in over two decades. Police tactics have drawn criticism following [USN:L6N45V0HM TEXT:"injuries"] among demonstrators, including a teenager who lost a hand after picking up a stun grenade. The police watchdog is investigating at least two dozen allegations of police violence. Lecornu said more than 900 police officers had also been injured in previous protests. Nunez said one person lost his hand in clashes with police on Saturday. French media reported he tried to pick up a stun grenade. The UNSA police union posted a video on X showing crowds attacking police vans with clubs and bricks in multiple locations. The union warned the government police forces were at breaking point. “Today again, in every corner of France, our colleagues are being used as punching bags. Pelted with stones, injured, trapped in real ambushes,” the union said. “Let everyone take responsibility: this cannot go on indefinitely. The rope is stretched to its maximum."

As President Donald Trump seeks greater influence over how elections are run, election officials across the country are bracing for disputes over voting, ballot counting and the certification of results. item.title: Pope Leo XIV to be discharged from hospital after successful lung cancer surgery on Saturday
item.description: Pope Leo XIV will leave the hospital on Saturday after four days of recovery from lung cancer surgery. The 71-year-old pontiff is expected to lead Sunday's traditional blessing, following a steady ...
item.content:encoded:
Pope Leo XIV to be discharged from hospital after successful lung cancer surgery on Saturday Pope Leo XIV will leave the hospital on Saturday after four days of recovery from lung cancer surgery. The 71-year-old pontiff is expected to lead Sunday's traditional blessing, following a steady recovery that included celebrating Mass and speaking with global leaders. ANI | Updated: 17-10-2026 17:19 IST | Created: 17-10-2026 17:19 IST

Pope Leo XIV (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Pope Leo XIV is scheduled to leave the hospital on Saturday afternoon following a four-day recovery from lung cancer surgery, with physicians declaring him “fit for discharge from the hospital” after evaluating his condition alongside blood tests and a morning chest X-ray, according to the Vatican. The 71-year-old pontiff is slated to recite the traditional blessing from a window overlooking St Peter’s Square on Sunday, marking his initial public appearance since entering Rome’s Gemelli Hospital. On Tuesday, Leo underwent a procedure to remove the lower lobe of his right lung after medical staff identified a suspected cancerous nodule. Subsequent examination confirmed the diagnosis as adenocarcinoma, which represents the most frequent form of lung cancer. According to a bulletin issued by his personal physician and surgeon, the pontiff was cleared to leave the medical facility following an evaluation of Saturday morning’s clinical findings and diagnostic results. Throughout his hospital stay, Leo has demonstrated progressive healing. His activities included a telephone conversation with Russian President Vladimir Putin, discussions with senior aides and the celebration of Mass inside a hospital chapel. On Friday, the Vatican published the first photographs of the pope following the operation, depicting him standing before an altar while wearing green vestments. During the service, Leo administered Communion to healthcare professionals and Vatican gendarmes. Vatican spokesperson Matteo Bruni noted that the pontiff expressed gratitude to the hospital personnel for “the work they do every day taking care of the sick in their fragility, and in a particular way what they had done for him”. Medical specialists continue to await laboratory findings to determine the exact molecular and genetic profile of the cancer, whether metastasis occurred beyond the excised lung lobe and whether additional therapy will be necessary. Leo retains an upcoming itinerary for a journey to Latin America scheduled between November 6 and 17. The visit involves numerous flights and helicopter transits, leaving approximately three weeks for convalescence after discharge. The Vatican has released a list of journalists accredited for the journey, signalling that preparations remain active. (ANI)

FAST

MANILA, Oct 17 : Multilateral development banks (MDBs) will strengthen efforts to help mineral-rich developing economies add more value to their resources by moving beyond extraction into processing, refining and manufacturing, according to an outline of a critical minerals collaboration framework published on Saturday. • The banks involved include the World Bank, the African Development Bank, the Asian Development Bank, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the European Investment Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank, according to the outline • The October framework calls for coordinated support across critical mineral supply chains, including financing, infrastructure and policy aimed at creating jobs, boosting domestic value addition, attracting private investment and supporting low-carbon transition • MDBs plan to support mineral corridors incorporating power, transport, logistics, water and digital infrastructure, while strengthening project preparation and using co-financing, guarantees and other financing tools to mobilise capital and accelerate private sector investments

item.title: Apple appoints Meta veteran Scott Tucker to lead global litigation
item.description: Tucker will oversee commercial and patent litigation worldwide and legal matters involving Apple's financial services as the company faces mounting lawsuits under General Counsel Jennifer Newstead ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Mark Gurman Apple Inc. has tapped a longtime Meta Platforms Inc. executive as its new litigation chief, bolstering its legal team at a time when the iPhone maker faces a growing array of lawsuits. The company has hired Scott Tucker, a longtime deputy general counsel and litigation chief at Meta, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The move reunites Tucker with new Apple General Counsel Jennifer Newstead, who is bringing on a trusted lieutenant from her time at the social networking giant. Tucker is becoming Apple’s vice president of global litigation and financial services, a newly created position overseeing commercial and patent litigation worldwide, said the people, who asked not to be named because the move isn’t public. He’ll also manage legal matters involving the company’s financial offerings.  The appointment means Heather Grenier, Apple’s current vice president of commercial and competition litigation, will move one level lower in the organisation, reporting to Tucker instead of directly to Newstead. Grenier will still remain on Newstead’s legal leadership team.  Tucker, in addition to his tenure at Meta, previously held a senior legal position at Morgan Stanley, giving him experience relevant to his new financial services responsibilities. Newstead took over as Apple’s general counsel in March after serving as Meta’s top lawyer for six years. Kyle Andeer, another senior member of Apple’s legal department and its longtime vice president managing regulatory and product-related legal matters, is seeing his role expand. He is gaining oversight of international legal matters and functions involving online child safety, cybersecurity and law enforcement. Spokespeople for Apple and Meta declined to comment.  The changes are part of a broader reorganisation under Newstead, who oversees legal and government affairs. Apple recently hired Nate Gatten, a former American Airlines Group Inc. executive, as its vice president of government affairs. The company has also appointed new government affairs leads for different international regions. Apple combined its legal and government affairs groups under Newstead following the recent retirements of Lisa Jackson, the former head of environmental, policy and social initiatives, and previous top lawyer Kate Adams. Former Chief Executive Officer Tim Cook, now the company’s executive chairman, has also taken a leading role in government affairs. Apple is waging a variety of legal battles, including a sweeping US antitrust lawsuit, its long-running dispute with Epic Games Inc. over App Store restrictions, and litigation related to privacy and delays to Siri features. The company has faced billions of dollars in judgments and settlements in recent years, while regulators in the US and Europe have challenged business practices central to the iPhone maker’s operations. Some Apple executives believe the company hasn’t fared as well in court as it should have, particularly in litigation involving the App Store. Those setbacks have forced Apple to change its commission structure and the circumstances under which it can charge developers. The changes threaten to significantly slow growth in Apple’s services business, a key driver of revenue expansion in recent years. A slowdown in that business would deal a major blow to the company’s overall financial performance. Even in the best of times, overseeing Apple’s litigation is a difficult job. The Cupertino, California-based company is among the most frequently sued businesses in the world, facing cases ranging from slip-and-fall claims at its retail stores to multibillion-dollar antitrust disputes. Grenier took over the role under particularly challenging circumstances, replacing her predecessor just before Apple’s landmark trial against Epic Games began in 2021. Her tenure has also spanned two major leadership transitions: the appointment of John Ternus as CEO and Newstead’s arrival. In recent weeks, Ternus has overseen a sweeping series of executive changes, including the appointment of new leaders for the App Store, events and corporate functions such as information security and real estate. The reshuffling also includes the departure of the longtime Apple Pay chief, the replacement of the company’s mergers and acquisitions head, and a reorganisation of the company’s hardware engineering division.

item.title: サッカー＝インテル、主将マルティネスが負傷で7試合欠場へ─報道
item.description: ［１６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１６日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイタリア・セリエＡ、インテルの主将ラウタロ・マルティネスがハムストリングの負傷により今後７試合を欠場する見通しとなった。米スポーツ専門局ＥＳＰＮが１６日に伝えた。

マルティネスは１３日にホームで行われた欧州チャンピオンズリーグ（ＣＬ）、３─４で敗れたクラブ・ブルージュ（ベルギー）戦にフル出場し、２得点を記録。しかし、１５日に行った検査の結果、左ハムストリングの肉離れが判明した。

インテルのクリスティアン・キブ監督は１６日、「彼はしばらく離脱することになる。私は医師ではないが、復帰までの目安は聞いている。おそらく代表戦期間明けには戻ってくるだろう」と述べた。

これにより、マルティネスは１７日のボローニャ戦と、２１日のＣＬシャフタル・ドネツク（ウクライナ）戦の欠場が確実となった。１１月の代表戦期間までには、３１日に行われるＡＣミランとのダービーを含め、７試合が予定されている。

マルティネスは今季、公式戦７試合に出場して６得点を記録。昨季はセリエＡで１７ゴールを挙げ、自身２回目となるリーグ得点王に輝いている。

item.title: イエメン・アデン空港にミサイル、サウジ向け弾道弾は迎撃
item.description: [１７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[１７日 ロイター] - イエメンのアデン国際空港に１６日、ミサイルが着弾した。一方、サウジアラビア主導の連合軍は、紅海沿岸の都市ヤンブーに向かっていた弾道ミサイルを迎撃したと発表した。

連合軍はさらに紅海上空で巡航ミサイル２発、サウジ南部とリヤド地方で無人機（ドローン）３機を破壊したと発表した。攻撃主体は明らかにしなかった。

イエメン南部アデンの治安当局によると、空港の敷地内にミサイル２発が着弾した。死傷者は報告されていない。当局は親イラン武装組織フーシ派による攻撃だと主張し、同空港への攻撃は１週間足らずで２回目だと説明した。

ヤンブーはサウジの重要な石油輸出拠点で、同国はここから紅海経由で原油を国際市場に送ることで、ホルムズ海峡を迂回できる。

サウジの民間防衛当局は１７日未明、イエメン国境に近い南西部アブハに警報を出し、その後解除した。これに先立ち、ジザン地方と南西部のハミースムシャイトにも警報を出していた。

フーシ派系メディアは１７日未明、イエメン北西部サアダの東で攻撃があったと報じた。サウジ主導の連合軍は、同地域で弾道ミサイル発射装置２基を破壊したと発表した。

item.title: Beijing Seeks Tighter Grip on AI Exports Amid U.S. Rivalry
item.description: By Eduardo Baptista China proposed export controls on 23 AI technologies on Friday, including those involving models, agents, and computing clusters, in a move to limit transfers of tools it views as vital to national security and to counter geopolitical competition with Washington. The proposals …
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
By Eduardo Baptista

China proposed export controls on 23 AI technologies on Friday, including those involving models, agents, and computing clusters, in a move to limit transfers of tools it views as vital to national security and to counter geopolitical competition with Washington.

The proposals cover overseas deployment of AI models containing restricted technology, but exclude access through application programming interfaces (APIs), websites, apps and software-as-a-service platforms, China’s commerce ministry said.

The distinction could let Chinese AI developers such as DeepSeek and Alibaba keep expanding internationally while giving Beijing greater oversight of transfers of sensitive AI technology abroad.

Chinese AI models have gained ground abroad thanks to lower prices and improving capabilities since DeepSeek’s R1 model emerged early last year, raising the stakes for Beijing as it decides how tightly to guard the sector.

Reuters reported in July that Chinese authorities had discussed with major technology companies, including Alibaba, ByteDance and Z.AI, potentially restricting overseas access to China’s most advanced AI models, including unreleased ones.

Preventing AI From Harming National Security

Frontier models like Anthropic’s Mythos have shown AI’s potential to turbocharge cyberattacks, worrying Beijing and prompting Chinese companies to develop their own versions.

Washington’s export controls on China’s access to cutting-edge American AI chips needed to train frontier models have so far helped keep US firms Anthropic and OpenAI in the lead, though Chinese rivals are finding workarounds to narrow the gap.

While both countries strive to lead in AI, some bilateral efforts are underway to address the existential risks the technology poses. The two powers have agreed to keep humans in control of nuclear-weapons decisions and last month set up a dialogue and an incident-communications channel for advanced AI.

The commerce ministry said on Friday the controls were partly intended to prevent misuse of AI technologies, including systems capable of autonomously generating and modifying malicious software that could threaten critical infrastructure and national security.

It said most AI technologies would remain freely exportable, with simplified licensing for open-source technology exports and Chinese companies operating their own computing centers overseas. Technology already in the public domain through open-source releases or academic papers would be outside the proposed controls.

Broader Revision

The proposals form part of a broader revision of China’s technology export catalog, covering 40 technologies across AI, biotechnology and solar power.

The proposals also include a ban on transferring intellectual property ownership for some novel cell and gene therapies and small interfering RNA (siRNA) technologies.

Exporters must register certain overseas technology transfers from Friday, pending final rules after public consultation on the proposals closes November 15.

item.title: Trump threatens California officials with imprisonment over stance on mail ballots
item.description: The Justice Dept. said election officials could be liable as abettors of a federal crime.
item.dc:creator: Jasper Ward
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department on Friday warned Los Angeles County and California election officials they could be liable as abettors of a federal crime if they count mail ballots returned by more than 20,000 people the Trump administration says are probably noncitizens. The warning to the Los Angeles County Assistant Counsel Peter Bollinger came less than three weeks before the November 3 midterm elections and days after the department gave California [USN:L6N460192 TEXT:"48 hours"] to review a list of alleged noncitizen voters or face legal action. On Thursday, the Justice Department [USN:L6N46117W TEXT:"sued California"] to block the state from counting the ballots. "Noncitizen voting in a federal election is a federal crime — and knowingly facilitating such conduct is equally unlawful," Trent McCotter, the acting US deputy attorney general, wrote in a letter released on Friday. McCotter called on the county and California's secretary of state to reconsider their refusal to take steps that the Trump administration argues are needed to deter voter fraud. US President Donald Trump shared the letter on Truth Social with the comment: "They will all go to jail for a long period of time!!!" California Secretary of State Shirley Weber and Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder Dean Logan were copied on McCotter's letter. The county's counsel office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Weber's office referred Reuters to an earlier statement in which she said the Justice Department's attempts to "unlawfully gain access to states' protected voter data and purge voter rolls serve only to cause chaos and fuel public distrust in our elections." An earlier letter that McCotter sent on Tuesday to Weber and Logan said the Justice Department provided officials in Los Angeles County with a "password-protected thumb drive" with the names of people the federal government "believes are likely noncitizens" that were sent mail-in ballots from California. Los Angeles County Counsel Dawyn R. Harrison said on Thursday the county cannot comply with the Justice Department's requests because the Trump administration did not explain how the list was made. Friday's letter from McCotter said the Justice Department used "internal immigration records" and data matching. In July, Trump said his administration had uncovered [USN:L1N43I0TJ TEXT:"evidence"] of more than 275,000 non-citizens registered to vote, but it was not clear how many had actually voted. In some previous cases, systems intended to verify citizenship have mistakenly flagged some naturalized US citizens as noncitizens. Studies have found that noncitizens casting actual ballots is exceedingly uncommon. Since July, the Justice Department has [USN:L6N45F10R TEXT:"ramped up prosecutions"] of people accused of illegally voting while not holding US citizenship. The White House has also [USN:L6N45D0T4 TEXT:"pushed"] federal agencies to accelerate their review of at least 47 state voter rolls obtained by the Department of Homeland Security, according to an internal email seen by Reuters.

item.title: India's 'cockroach' movement founder released a day after detention
item.description: India's "cockroach" youth movement leader was released by an Indian court on Saturday, a day after he was detained for trying to lead another protest rally in New Delhi calling for the resignation of the country's election chief.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's "cockroach" youth movement leader was released by an Indian court on Saturday, a day after he was detained for trying to lead another protest rally in New Delhi calling for the resignation of the country's election chief. Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), rose to prominence this year when a weeks-long sit-in contributed to India's education minister resigning. CJP's legal affairs head Ratna Singh said Dipke was released after he agreed to certain conditions. Singh gave no details of the terms. Dipke's youth-led group, opposition parties and student organisations have held near-daily protests this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner [USN:P8N44T0DC TEXT:"Gyanesh Kumar's"] resignation over a revision of [USN:L1N45V037 TEXT:"voter lists"] that they say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). More than 130 million voters were deleted during the revision. The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes. Student activist Neha Bora, a prominent face of the protests, who was also detained on Friday as she tried to reach central Delhi with dozens of supporters, was released on Saturday. "Please, spare the people of India. Impeach Gyanesh Kumar and halt SIR (special intensive revision), so that the ordinary citizens of this country can breathe a sigh of relief, feel at ease, and have their voting rights ensured," Bora told ANI news agency after she was released. STUDENT GROUPS CALL FOR MORE PROTEST ACTION Dipke was [USN:L6N4620GJ TEXT:"detained"] on Friday as he stepped out of a house in central Delhi, with police hauling him into a police car and driving away after a brief argument. Dipke had called Friday's protest in support of two CJP leaders detained and sent to jail this week for five days for demonstrating at a protest site in violation of a ban. Earlier on Friday, police had met Dipke and warned him against going ahead with the protest. Student groups called for more protest action on Saturday. The movement, which was mobilised by the youth and joined by many opposition parties, has emerged as one of the biggest political challenges faced by Modi and the BJP in the prime minister's 12 years in power.

item.title: サッカー＝チェルシー主将ジェームズ、膝の手術で数週間離脱
item.description: ［ロンドン １６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ロンドン　１６日　ロイター］　 - サッカーのイングランド・プレミアリーグ、チェルシーを率いるシャビアロンソ監督は１６日、練習中に膝を負傷した同クラブの主将リース・ジェームズ（２６）が軽度の手術を受け、戦列を離れると明かした。

シャビアロンソ監督は１７日に敵地で行われるプレミアリーグのエバートン戦に向けた記者会見で、「彼は代表戦期間明けから良いスタートを切りたがっていたが、直近の練習で負傷してしまった。手術は無事に成功した。具体的な復帰時期は定めていないが、数週間の離脱となるだろう」と述べた。

英メディアによれば、離脱期間は３カ月となる見込み。ジェームズはここ数シーズンにわたって度重なるけがに悩まされており、直近の代表戦でも負傷のためイングランド代表メンバーから外れていた。

item.title: サッカー＝ウルグアイで「電子カード」試験導入、警告をデジタル表示
item.description: ［１６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１６日　ロイター］ - サッカーのウルグアイ・カップ（杯）で１５日、審判員が従来のイエローカードに代わり、スマートフォンほどの大きさの電子機器を使って選手に警告を与える試みが行われた。審判業務のデジタル化を目指す取り組みの一環。

審判員が電子機器を使用すると、警告などの懲戒処分がデジタルで記録される。機器は試合中の出来事を時刻とともに記録する仕組みで、ウルグアイ・サッカー協会が使用する「ＣＯＭＥＴ」と呼ばれるシステムへの公式記録の提出を効率化する狙いがある。

実際に使用した審判員は、機器は使いやすくてソフトウエアの反応も速かったと評価。「素早くカードを提示する際の魔法のような魅力は少し失われるが、特に事務作業の面で大いに役立つと思う」と述べた。

ただ、試験運用では視認性の問題も浮上した。以前の試験では日光で画面が見えにくくなり中止されたほか、１５日の試合でも観客やテレビ視聴者が判定を識別しにくい場面があった。開発側は機器の周囲にＬＥＤ照明を取り付けるなど、色の識別を容易にする改良を検討している。

item.title: Zelenskiy criticizes Trump's waiver of sanctions on Russia as 'wrong'
item.description: 'It definitely helps only the Russians,' Zelenskiy wrote on social media.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh, Jasper Ward
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump's decision to waive sanctions and tariffs on Russia days before they were to take effect will "unfortunately" lead to additional relief for Russia and lead to further Russian aggression, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy posted on Saturday. "The decision to undo all of this, to block all of it, seems wrong to me," Zelenskiy wrote on X. "It definitely helps only the Russians." An executive order issued by Trump on Friday night waived key Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs — including duties on the country's goods and penalties for buying its oil and gas — that had been scheduled to start next week under the legislation known as [USN:L6N45A18J TEXT:"the Graham Act"] that he signed into law last month. Trump said the waiver was in the national interests of the United States. The law is meant to increase pressure on Russia for its invasion of Ukraine that began in 2022. Trump, however, has been warming toward Moscow while publicly criticizing Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, including suggesting Kyiv needs a new leader. Zelenskiy said Trump's latest action emboldens Russian President Vladimir Putin and encourages more attacks by Russia. "It only fuels their satisfaction and their desire to keep killing people," wrote Zelenskiy, who said Russia on Friday struck more than 15 Ukrainian power generation and transmission sites. "This certainly does not stop the war." The Ukrainian leader accused Russia of planning to ramp up strikes in western Ukraine. "Is Russia preparing for this? I think so," Zelenskiy wrote. Russia's investment envoy, Kirill Dmitriev, on Friday called the Trump waiver "a truly historic moment," posting on X that had the penalties taken effect, they could have effectively brought all economic cooperation between Russia and the US to a halt. Weeks before US midterm elections in which Trump's Republicans are battling to maintain their narrow grip on both chambers of Congress, the new measures could have risked further [USN:L6N45A18J TEXT:"raising oil prices"] as Americans face increased costs largely attributed to the US-Israeli war on Iran, analysts have said. Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 in mid-September. The [USN:L6N45A18J TEXT:"legislation,"] whose primary backer in Congress was the late Senator Lindsey Graham, a South Carolina Republican, would have imposed tariffs of up to 100% within 30 days on all goods brought into the US from the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or gas, as well as any country that knowingly bought oil or gas 30 days after the law was enacted or was among the top five countries helping Russia evade sanctions. Countries such as China and [USN:L1N45G03K TEXT:"India"], which are among the biggest buyers of Russian oil, however, had raised concerns about the Graham Act. Beijing has said it "consistently opposed long-arm jurisdiction that lacks a basis in international law" while India warned Washington that new tariffs could impact bilateral ties. But the Graham Act also allows the president to waive sanctions by informing Congress that he has determined that they are not in the national interest. Friday's executive order said the waiver will remain in effect until Trump or his top officials determine that "further action is appropriate." US Representative Don Beyer, a Virginia Democrat, said Trump was giving in to Putin. "Trump's latest surrender to Putin again betrays our Ukrainian partners and defies clear congressional intent of legislation designed to punish Russia for its illegal war of aggression," Beyer said in a statement on Friday. Graham, who died in July, strongly supported US assistance to Ukraine. The passage of the bill named for him had provided hope that there would be continued bipartisan support for Kyiv, wrote Zelenskiy, who lamented the late senator's absence. "It’s difficult without him, I’ll be honest," Zelenskiy posted on Saturday. The Ukrainian leader predicted that the US under Trump will continue sanctions relief for Russia beyond Friday's waiver and the [USN:L8N4610WB TEXT:"diesel export agreement"] announced earlier this month. "I think the diesel deal and the move regarding the Lindsey Graham Act are not the end of it. Unfortunately," Zelenskiy wrote.

item.title: Bangladesh is battling measles. It's a 'real warning' to other nations
item.description: Bangladesh's vaccination program was a success story until it faltered because of political turmoil. Its unvaccinated children are paying the price.
item.dc:creator: Ruma Paul, Jennifer Rigby, Sam Jahan, Zia Chowdhury
item.content:encoded: The parents of Labiba Akter have kept a blue dress once worn by their nine-month-old daughter, who died of measles in June, as a keepsake. They were not told she was eligible for a vaccination before she contracted the disease. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain Bangladesh is battling to contain the world’s worst measles outbreak , a crisis exacerbated by weak data, inadequate outreach and vaccination gaps that experts say offers a warning to other nations about the deadly risk of falling immunisation rates. Bangladesh, whose routine vaccination programme faltered in 2025, reported 202,000 suspected measles cases – 22,000 of them laboratory-confirmed – since the start of the outbreak in mid-March to October 9, the World Health Organization said. That’s more suspected cases than any other country this year. So far, 1,147 people have died of the highly contagious disease, with 94% of reported deaths among children under five years old, the WHO said. Bangladesh's experience shows the challenge of containing an outbreak when vaccination coverage falls below 95%, a level the WHO says is needed to prevent outbreaks. Bangladesh almost achieved that in recent years but in 2025 coverage dropped. A Reuters review of WHO documents, alongside interviews with more than a dozen scientists, health workers and officials, shows Bangladesh was also hampered in its emergency response by data that left out millions of children, shortcomings in preparation and a failure to reach enough parents. "This is a real warning to every country," said Mark Jit, a WHO vaccine adviser and professor at the School of Global Public Health at New York University. Preventing an outbreak through vaccinations was easier, cheaper and safer than responding to an emergency, he said. "The response will stop the outbreak eventually, but in the meantime, many will have had measles, and some will have died," he said. Ziauddin Hyder, special assistant on health affairs to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, told Reuters in September the government was doing everything it could to end the outbreak. The government did not respond to further questions sent in October for this article. Amin Mia and Sajina Begum pose with their four-year-old daughter who survived measles. Below, Sajina Begum shows a photo of her husband, daughter and two-year-old son, Arman Hossain, who died of the disease in July. Neither child received a vaccination. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain ‘THEY CAME ONLY AFTER I BURIED MY SON’ In the northeast Sylhet region, one of the worst-hit areas in the nation of 178 million people, two-year-old Arman Hossain died unvaccinated in July, 24 hours after admission to hospital for treatment paid for by selling the family's three-wheeled auto rickshaw. His unvaccinated four-year-old sister survived. His father Amin Mia, 26, said no health workers came to their remote village in Sylhet to offer vaccinations in time. "They came only after I buried my son," he said. Measles usually kills two or three people in every 1,000 cases, the WHO says, but the disease can be more deadly in poorer nations because of factors such as malnutrition. This is a real warning to every country. Mark Jit, a WHO vaccine adviser In the town of Chhatak, also in the Sylhet region, the daughter of 30-year-old carpenter Humayun Rashid died unvaccinated in June aged nine months. Labiba Akter could have received an inoculation in April when an emergency programme lowered the vaccination age to six months from nine. "No health worker came to tell us," her father said. In May, Health Minister Sardar Md. Sakhawat Husain said the emergency drive had brought cases in hotspots "almost to zero" and the outbreak was under control. Yet in September, Bangladesh reported a daily average of 1,198 new cases of measles, which causes a high fever, cough and telltale rash. That was the highest total since May. The Bangladesh outbreak comes as vaccine hesitancy is rising, particularly in wealthier nations, amid skepticism championed by figures such as US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. In Bangladesh, access to inoculations and awareness are bigger hurdles, experts said. Until recently, Bangladesh had been a vaccination success story. The WHO and the United Nations children’s agency UNICEF estimated that in 2024 it achieved 96% coverage for the first vaccine dose and 93% for the second, which is given to capture the small percentage of children who don't develop immunity after one shot. But that same year, protests erupted that ended 15 years of rule by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. In the ensuing political turmoil, health workers went on strike, vaccine orders were delayed and follow-up vaccinations that usually accompany routine programmes were disrupted. Nadia Akter Manna, the mother of Labiba Akter, shows a few personal items bought for her daughter before she died. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain Humayun Rashid, the father of Labiba Akter, works on his carpentry in September, three months after his daughter's death. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain In a report published in July this year, WHO and UNICEF estimated first-dose coverage in 2025 had fallen to 90%, while second-dose coverage was 86%, several percentage points below the 95% needed for herd immunity. The report also raised questions about the quality of official data on vaccinations for measles and other diseases for the years 2023 to 2025. It said preliminary figures sometimes showed numbers of those inoculated exceeded 100% of those targeted, indicating mistakes in counting doses or target numbers. EMERGENCY PROGRAMME MISSED MILLIONS Still, when the measles outbreak erupted, Bangladesh responded swiftly and initially seemed to be winning the battle. An emergency programme was followed by an initial slowdown in new cases after almost 20 million children received a vaccination in April and May. The government said it had covered every child in the target age group of six months to five years. But in reality the programme fell short. This emerged when another routine health intervention in June had a target list with 4 million more children than the measles campaign despite covering the same age group. "There is a gap," prime ministerial adviser Hyder told Reuters on September 14, as measles cases rose again, blaming vaccine hesitancy by parents or child illnesses for keeping kids away. Iqbal and Sharmin wait as their five-month-old son, Esa, receives treatment for measles in the neonatal intensive care unit of a hospital in Narayanganj, Bangladesh, May 11, 2026. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain Other challenges have also emerged. Documents detailing meetings in April and August between the government, the WHO and other health partners, reviewed by Reuters and not previously reported, show how efforts to act fast may have led to shortcomings. Minutes from the April 19 meeting outlined how the government opted for just one round of so-called readiness checks before launching its emergency vaccination programme due to time constraints, instead of the typical four rounds. Checks cover everything from ensuring fridges are available for keeping vaccines cool to determining how many children should be vaccinated. The single round of checks suggested most - but not all - districts were ready, according to the minutes. Eight-year-old Masum receives treatment in the overcrowded measles isolation ward of Shahid Shamsuddin Ahmed Hospital in Sylhet, one of the worst-hit areas in Bangladesh's measles outbreak. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain The 100-bed Shahid Shamsuddin Ahmed Hospital in the Sylhet region has been overwhelmed by measles cases. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain On the day Reuters visited the hospital in September, 178 patients were admitted. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain THE POOREST ‘PAY THE PRICE’ "When preparedness checks are not done properly, it is often the poorest and hardest-to-reach children who miss out on vaccination and pay the price," said Professor Mahmudur Rahman, an epidemiologist and chair of Bangladesh's National Verification Committee for Measles and Rubella Elimination. Hyder said the April campaign was launched in four weeks. Yet Tajul Islam Abdul Bari, who led immunisation in Bangladesh until 2017, said campaigns usually demand months of planning. By the August meeting, shortcomings in the rollout were identified. Minutes noted the proportion of children with confirmed measles cases who had not been vaccinated was "virtually unchanged between pre-campaign (82%) and post-campaign (85%) ... underscoring persistent coverage gaps". The WHO did not respond to questions about the April and August meetings. But deputy WHO representative to Bangladesh, Dr Rajesh Narwal, said the WHO was determined to support the government in its goal of vaccinating every child at risk. "Routine immunisation must become more effective and resilient so that these gaps do not develop again," he said. In Sylhet, where official records show 180 children have died, 8 of 16 families Reuters interviewed in September said they had not seen health workers offering vaccinations. At least six families said health workers visited only after a child had died from measles in their community. A measles survivor, two-year-old Al Raiyan Twoha sleeps on his mother Rajia Begum's shoulder in the Sylhet region of Bangladesh. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain At the end of September, the government launched a new campaign to target 3.4 million children previously missed. "We will involve people across villages so that no child is left behind," the health minister told a news conference. Yet reaching every child remains a challenge. UNICEF and the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics say as many as 40% of children go unregistered, while government data showed around a third of health worker posts are unfilled. Health experts are also pushing the government to expand the programme to vaccinate children over five. That age group represents a third of measles cases, the WHO says. In addition, scientists in Bangladesh are studying why immunity is waning faster than expected in babies up to six months or so. They are usually still protected by maternal antibodies, experts say. Ensuring prompt medical care is vital, the WHO says, another challenge for Bangladesh as it also fights a dengue epidemic . In September, every ward in Sylhet's 100-bed Shahid Shamsuddin Ahmed Hospital, which is treating measles, appeared overwhelmed. On the day Reuters visited, 178 patients were admitted. The blue dress of measles victim Labiba Akter hangs on a line in the village in Bangladesh’s Sylhet region where her parents live. REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain

item.title: テニス＝ジョコビッチ、スイス室内に15年ぶり参戦
item.description: ［１６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１６日　ロイター］ - 男子テニスで四大大会通算２４勝を誇るノバク・ジョコビッチ（セルビア）が２６日開幕のスイス室内（バーゼル）に主催者推薦で出場することが１６日、決まった。同大会への出場は２０１１年以来１５年ぶりで、４度目となる。

３９歳のジョコビッチは今季、１０月の中国オープンで自身が持つ大会最多優勝記録を更新する７度目のタイトルを獲得した一方、マスターズ上海大会では２回戦でフベルト・フルカチュ（ポーランド）に敗れるなど好不調の波がある。全米オープンでは四大大会で０６年全豪オープン以来となる初戦敗退を喫した。

ジョコビッチは上海大会で敗退した後、今季残りは１１月２─８日のパリ・マスターズと年間成績上位選手によるＡＴＰファイナルにのみ出場する予定だと語っていた。

ジョコビッチは現在、ＡＴＰファイナル出場権を争う年間ポイントランキングで１１位。世界ランキング１位のヤニク・シナー（イタリア）が長引く膝の負傷で今季残りの欠場を決めたため、１７回目の出場を果たすには年間９位以内に入る必要がある。

item.title: テニス＝マスターズ上海大会、メドベージェフとホダルが4強
item.description: ［上海 １６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［上海　１６日　ロイター］ - 男子テニスのマスターズ上海大会は１６日、シングルス準々決勝を行い、ロシア出身で第５シードのダニル・メドベージェフが第１５シードのトミー・ポール（米国）を６─３、１─６、６─３で下し、準決勝に進出した。

元世界ランキング１位のメドベージェフは１６本のサービスエース、３１本のウィナーを記録。ツアー通算７０回目の準決勝進出を決めた。

２０１９年大会覇者のメドベージェフは今大会で勝ち残っている唯一の歴代優勝者。準決勝では第１２シードのラファエル・ホダル（スペイン）と初対戦する。

２０歳のホダルは第２０シードのカスパー・ルード（ノルウェー）を４─６、６─４、６─３で破り、大会史上最年少の４強入りを果たした。今大会初出場のホダルは４試合連続で第１セットを落としてからの逆転勝利となった。

item.title: サッカー＝レアルがリーグ会長の辞任要求、ナチス宣伝手法との比較に反発
item.description: ［マドリード １６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［マドリード　１６日　ロイター］ - サッカーのスペイン１部レアル・マドリードは１６日、同リーグのハビエル・テバス会長がクラブ経営陣の言動をナチスの宣伝手法に例えたことを受け、同会長の辞任を要求した。

テバス会長は１６日、自身の交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）で、「レアル・マドリードの経営陣は代弁者たちのオーケストラを指揮しており、レアル・マドリードＴＶがそれを主導している」と記した。これは、テバス会長とリーグがレアル・マドリードの利益に反する行動を取っていると指摘した２人のジャーナリストの記事に対する反応だった。

さらに同会長は「彼らのやり方はいつも同じだ。自分たちに都合の良いプレー場面を選び出し、不満を繰り返し、疑念をあおり、敵を指弾する。この手法はナチス・ドイツのゲッベルスが用いた宣伝手法の仕組みをほうふつとさせる」とし、「私が比較したのはあくまで宣伝手法であり、イデオロギーやレアル・マドリードのファンのことではない」と付け加えた。

これに対し、レアル・マドリードは声明で、テバス会長がナチスの宣伝手法を引き合いに出したことは「容認し難く、極めて重大な事態だ」と批判した。「クラブ、経営陣、テレビ局の信用を傷つけようとした。テバス氏の度重なる言動は組織のトップとしての責任を果たす上で不可欠な中立性、敬意、公平性の欠如を示している」とした上で、リーグ会長とスペイン・サッカー連盟副会長を辞任するよう求めた。

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝ドジャースのロハスが現役引退、ワールドシリーズ2回制覇
item.description: ［１６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１６日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）ドジャースに所属するミゲル・ロハス内野手（３７）が１５日、現役引退を表明した。

ドジャースは同日、ナ・リーグ優勝決定シリーズ（７回戦制）第４戦でブルワーズに４─６で敗れ、４連敗で敗退。ワールドシリーズ３連覇の夢が絶たれた試合後、ロハスはチームメートに引退を伝えた。

ロハスは「これで終わりだ。人生、キャリア、野球界での次のステップに進む。今日が選手としてこのユニフォームとスパイクを身に着ける最後の日だった。今はスパイクを脱ぐのが本当につらい」と声を詰まらせながら語った。

ベネズエラ出身のロハスは２０１４年にドジャースでメジャーデビューし、その後マーリンズで８シーズンを過ごし、２３年にドジャースに復帰。２４、２５年のワールドシリーズ連覇を経験した。ＭＬＢ通算１３シーズンで１４０１試合に出場し、打率２割６分、１０４８安打、６１本塁打、３８６打点、６８盗塁を記録した。

２５年のワールドシリーズでは、ブルージェイズとの第７戦で九回に同点本塁打を放ち、優勝に大きく貢献。ドジャース復帰後の４シーズンでは４４６試合に出場し、打率２割６分を記録した。

引退後はドジャースの選手育成部門に加わる予定で、具体的な役職は今後決まる。

前半３分に堂安、同９分に小杉がチャンスに絡んだフランクフルトだが、０─０のまま後半へ。それでも、迎えた後半３２分にペナルティーエリア右でパスを受けたユネス・エブヌタリブがシュートを沈め、これを決勝点とした。

フランクフルトは３試合ぶりの勝利。勝ち点８とし、暫定８位に順位を上げた。

item.title: ゴルフ＝原と竹田が首位と3打差の4位、ビュイックＬＰＧＡ
item.description: ［１６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１６日　ロイター］ - 米女子ゴルフのビュイックＬＰＧＡは１６日、中国・上海の佘山国際ＧＣ（パー７２）で第２ラウンドを行い、原英莉花と竹田麗央が通算３アンダーの４位で並び、首位と３打差につけた。

前日７位の原は５バーディー、５ボギーの７２で回り、３位スタートの竹田は３バーディー、４ボギーの７３とスコアを１つ落とし、原と同じ通算１４１となった。

１２位で出た勝みなみは７８と崩れ、通算４オーバーの３０位に後退。吉田優利は４０位、西郷真央は５１位となった。

前日首位のチェ・ヘジン（韓国）は７４とスコアを２つ落としたものの、通算６アンダーの１３８で単独首位を維持。グレース・キム（オーストラリア）が７２、エイミー・ヤン（韓国）が７１で回り、ともに通算４アンダーの２位につけた。

item.title: サッカー＝上田、ＡＦＣ最優秀国際選手の候補入り
item.description: ［１６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１６日　ロイター］ - アジア・サッカー連盟（ＡＦＣ）は１６日、２０２６年の年間表彰候補者を発表し、男子の最優秀国際選手賞で日本代表ＦＷ上田綺世（リール）が名を連ねた。

上田は昨季、オランダ１部フェイエノールトで得点王に輝き、今夏のワールドカップ（Ｗ杯）北中米大会でも２得点を記録。韓国代表の黄仁範、前回受賞者の李康仁と共にノミネートされた。

女子の最優秀国際選手賞には長谷川唯が３年連続で候補入り。オーストラリア代表のアランナ・ケネディ、ケイトリン・フォードと選ばれた。

男子の年間最優秀監督賞には、Ｊ１町田の黒田剛監督とＵ─１７（１７歳以下）女子日本代表の白井貞義監督が入った。

男子の年間最優秀若手選手賞では、北原槙、市原吏音、佐藤龍之介の日本人３選手が候補を独占。女子では福島望愛が候補入りした。

表彰式は１１月１９日にタイの首都バンコクで開催され、計１９部門の受賞者が発表される。

Oct 16 : Anthropic has signed a lease with EverWind for data center capacity at Point Tupper, Nova Scotia, marking the Claude maker’s first data center agreement in Canada, a company executive said on Friday. Here are some more details: • Separately, EverWind unveiled plans to invest more than C$10 billion in the data center campus and wind power projects in Nova Scotia, calling it the largest privately funded investment in the province’s history. • Data centers have faced criticism over their heavy power and water use and the strain they place on local infrastructure.

item.title: 海外勢の米国債保有、8月は9.33兆ドルに増加 英加がけん引
item.description: [ニューヨーク １６日 ロイター] - 米財務省が１６日発表した８月の対米証券投資統計によると、海外勢の米国債保有残...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
海外勢の米国債保有、8月は9.33兆ドルに増加　英加がけん引 10/17 6:34 配信

米ドル紙幣。３月撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

[ニューヨーク １６日 ロイター] - 米財務省が１６日発表した８月の対米証券投資統計によると、海外勢の米国債保有残高は９兆３３１０億ドルと、前月の９兆２４８０億ドルから増加した。２カ月連続の減少から増加に転じた。英国とカナダの保有が増加をけん引した。

前年同月比では１％弱の増加にとどまった。

日本の保有高は８月に１兆０６８０億ドルと、７月の１兆１０３０億ドルから３．２％減少し、４カ月連続の減少となった。ただ、日本は海外勢としては依然として米国債の最大保有国だ。保有額は２０２１年１１月に１兆３２５０億ドルでピークを付けた。

海外勢の保有額で２位の英国は、８月の保有高が前月の９９８３億ドルから１．１％増の１兆００９０億ドルとなり、初めて１兆ドルの大台を突破した。

中国の保有高は５９０７億ドルと、７月の６１８０億ドルから２．４％減少し、２００８年８月以来の低水準となった。減少は３カ月連続となった。中国は海外勢の保有額で依然として３位だが、８月の保有額は前年比で約１６％減少した。

米国債は１０８９億ドルの買い越しとなった。７月は３６億ドルの売り越しだった。

米社債は４１６億ドルの買い越しとなり、前月の２６９億ドルから増加した。

対米証券投資は１９９８億ドルの買い越し。前月の８７４億ドルから増加した。

item.description: [ソウル １７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ソウル １７日 ロイター] - 北朝鮮の国営朝鮮中央通信（ＫＣＮＡ）は１７日、北朝鮮が１５日に新型魚雷兵器システムの水中実験を行い、技術的な改良を検証したと報じた。実験は成功し、同国の海軍力発展における重要な一歩を刻んだとしている。

ＫＣＮＡによると、実験では過去５年間に１８０回以上の試験を通じて開発された推進技術が検証された。新型の高速精密誘導魚雷には、目標の探知・誘導に人工知能（ＡＩ）が使用されたという。

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ市場サマリー（16日）10年債利回り週間で大幅低下、ドル軟調　株反落 10/17 6:10 配信

＜為替＞　ドルが円やユーロなどの主要通貨に対して下落した。米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の追加利上げ観測の後退に加え、ＡＩ（人工知能）関連銘柄主導の株安への懸念が引き続き重しになっている。    米国では今週発表された９月の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）と９月の卸売物価指数（ＰＰＩ）をが予想を上回って伸びたことなどで、一時的に利上げ観測が再燃。ただその後、ＦＲＢ当局者の発言で追加利上げを急がない姿勢が示されたことで、ドル相場に対する支援材料も薄れていた。    今週はこのほか、ＡＩ関連銘柄が大幅に下落。ＡＩ関連銘柄やサプライチェーン全体に資金を投じてきた投資家の間でデータセンター運営企業が債務返済に必要な利益を十分なタイミングで確保できるのか疑念が広がっていることが背景にあり、影響はドル相場にも波及している。    ウォーシュＦＲＢ議長はバンコクで開かれた国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）・世界銀行年次総会で行った講演で、米経済の力強さについて楽観的な見方を示すとともに、エネルギーショックが続きインフレ抑制に向けた金融引き締めが行われる中でも、世界経済が持ちこたえていることに驚きを表明。ＦＲＢの金融政策については「予断を持たない」と述べるにとどめ、追加利上げの可能性について手掛かりは示さなかった。    ＣＭＥフェドウオッチによると、今月の会合で金利据え置きが決定される確率は８３％。１カ月前の４９％から大きく上昇した。    終盤の取引で、ドル／円は０．０８％安の１ドル＝１５８．１１円。日銀の植田和男総裁は１６日、基調的な物価上昇率について、２％に「かなり近づいている」と指摘する一方で、２％目標に到達したかの判断は２９日からの金融政策決定会合で「政策委員の間でしっかり議論して結論を出したい」と述べるにとどめた。    ユーロ／ドルは０．０８％高の１．１２２７ドル。    主要６通貨に対するドル指数は０．１７％安の１０１．８７。

ＮＹ外為市場：[USD/J]

＜債券＞　指標となる１０年債利回りが週間ベースで１年超ぶりの低下幅となる見通しとなった。足元の経済指標を見極める動きが見られる中、市場では米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の次回利上げは１２月まで見送られるとの見方が強まっている。    午後の取引で１０年債利回りは横ばいの５．０８７％。一時、５．１３３４％まで上昇していた。ただ、週間ベースでは、２０２５年８月１日終了週以来の低下幅となる見通しとなった。    この日発表の経済指標では、９月の米輸入物価指数は前年比で８．１％上昇と、２０２２年７月以来の大幅な伸びとなった。中東紛争が続く中、インフレ圧力が高まっていることを改めて示唆した。    ＦＲＢのウォーシュ議長は１６日、バンコクで開かれた国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）・世界銀行年次総会で、金利決定については「予断を持たない」と表明。今月の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で利上げするか、据え置くかについては手掛かりを示さなかった。    市場ではＦＲＢが１０月２７─２８日のＦＯＭＣで金利を据え置くとの見方が一段と強まり、ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、市場が織り込む据え置きの確率は約８３％、１２月の利上げ確率は約８８％となった。    ２年債利回りは３．２ｂｐ低下の４．７１９％。一時、４．７８３％まで上昇していた。    ３０年債利回りは０．５ｂｐ上昇の５．４３３％。一時、５．４６４％を付けていた。     ２年債と１０年債の利回り格差は３６．６ｂｐ。    物価連動国債（ＴＩＰＳ）と通常の国債の利回り差で期待インフレを示すブレーク・イーブン・インフレ率（ＢＥＩ）は、１０年物が２．３４７％となった。

米金融・債券市場：[US/BJ]

＜株式＞　反落して取引を終えた。人工知能（ＡＩ）向けクラウドサービス大手コアウィーブやブロードコムなどＡＩ関連のハイテク株が再び売られたほか、原油価格の急伸も重しとなった。    エヌビディアが出資するコアウィーブは１２％下落。直近５営業日の下げ幅は約２５％となった。同社の社債は今週、大きく売り込まれ、利回りは１５％を超えた。    ブロードコムは４．５％下落。フィラデルフィア半導体指数は３．８％安となり、２００８年以来となる８営業日続落となった。    ナスダック総合は週前半からの下落幅を拡大した。多額の債務を抱えるＡＩインフラ企業が、借り入れコストの上昇が見込まれる中、債務返済に見合うだけの利益を期日までに計上できないのではないかとの懸念が圧迫した。     Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種の主要１１業種のうち６つが上昇。エネルギーが２．４７％上昇でトップ、公益事業が１．４％上昇と続いた。    その他の個別銘柄では、電気自動車（ＥＶ）大手テスラは３．１％下落。同社は、ロケットのような推進装置（スラスター）を搭載した新デザインのスポーツカー「ロードスター」を公開し、２０２８年に生産を開始すると発表した。    動画配信大手ネットフリックスは２．８％下落。同社は、最高コンテンツ責任者として元ディズニー幹部のピーター・ライス氏を起用すると発表した。    来週からは第３・四半期決算シーズンが本格化し、テスラ、メタ・プラットフォームズ、プロクター・アンド・ギャンブルなどが決算を控える。ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、アナリストは四半期利益がＡＩ関連の大型株にけん引され、平均で３０％超急増すると予想している。    Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種では値下がり銘柄数と値上がり銘柄数がほぼ拮抗した。    米取引所の合算出来高は１８６億株。直近２０営業日の平均は１７７億株。

米国株式市場：[.NJP]

＜金先物＞　米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の追加利上げ観測が強まる中、金相場は小動きとなり、週間では下落の見通しとなった。中心限月１２月物の清算値は０．３％高の１オンス＝４１８１．１０ドル。金現物は、米東部時間午後２時７分（日本時間１７日午前３時７分）時点で０．１％安の１オンス＝４１６５．１２ドル。週間では０．７％下落した。

米卸売物価指数（ＰＰＩ）と消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）が予想を上回る伸びを示したことで、ＦＲＢによる年内追加利上げの可能性が意識されている。ＦＲＢのウォーシュ議長は米経済の強さに楽観的な見方を示したものの、利上げ方針については明言しなかった。市場では今月の利上げは見送られるとの見方が大勢だが、１２月の利上げ確率は９０％とされている。

ＮＹ貴金属：[GOL/XJ]

＜米原油先物＞　大幅高となり、北海ブレントが一時１バレル＝１１０ドルと５月以来の高値を付けた。中東情勢の緊迫化で供給が一段と逼迫するとの懸念が広がったほか、ロシアからの世界市場向けディーゼル燃料の供給能力に不透明感が強まったことが背景。    清算値は、北海ブレント先物が３．９４ドル（３．７％）高の１０９．８６ドルで、５月１９日以来の高値。米ＷＴＩ先物は３．４４ドル（３．５％）高の１０１．４１ドルで、９月１７日以来の高値となった。    今週に入ってブレントは４．９％、ＷＴＩは１０．４％、それぞれ上昇した。

ＮＹＭＥＸエネルギー：[CR/USJ]

item.content:encoded:
米国株式市場＝反落、ＡＩ関連株の売り継続　コアウィーブ12％安 10/17 6:00 配信

米ニューヨーク証券取引所（NYSE）の取引フロア。2025年9月撮影。REUTERS/Jeenah Moon

Noel Randewich

[１６日　ロイター] - 米国株式市場は反落して取引を終えた。人工知能（ＡＩ）向けクラウドサービス大手コアウィーブやブロードコムなどＡＩ関連のハイテク株が再び売られたほか、原油価格の急伸も重しとなった。

エヌビディアが出資するコアウィーブは１２％下落。直近５営業日の下げ幅は約２５％となった。同社の社債は今週、大きく売り込まれ、利回りは１５％を超えた。

ブロードコムは４．５％下落。フィラデルフィア半導体指数は３．８％安となり、２００８年以来となる８営業日続落となった。

ＵＳバンク・ウェルス・マネジメントのシニア投資ストラテジスト、ロブ・ハワース氏は「市場には幾分の警戒感がある。とりわけ原油高は、株式の株価収益率（ＰＥＲ）を圧迫しがちだ。投資家は週末に向けてリスクを取るよりも慎重な姿勢を取ろうとしている」と述べた。

ナスダック総合は週前半からの下落幅を拡大した。多額の債務を抱えるＡＩインフラ企業が、借り入れコストの上昇が見込まれる中、債務返済に見合うだけの利益を期日までに計上できないのではないかとの懸念が圧迫した。

Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種の主要１１業種のうち６つが上昇。エネルギーが２．４７％上昇でトップ、公益事業が１．４％上昇と続いた。

その他の個別銘柄では、電気自動車（ＥＶ）大手テスラは３．１％下落。同社は、ロケットのような推進装置（スラスター）を搭載した新デザインのスポーツカー「ロードスター」を公開し、２０２８年に生産を開始すると発表した。

動画配信大手ネットフリックスは２．８％下落。同社は、最高コンテンツ責任者として元ディズニー幹部のピーター・ライス氏を起用すると発表した。

来週からは第３・四半期決算シーズンが本格化し、テスラ、メタ・プラットフォームズ、プロクター・アンド・ギャンブルなどが決算を控える。ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、アナリストは四半期利益がＡＩ関連の大型株にけん引され、平均で３０％超急増すると予想している。

Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種では値下がり銘柄数と値上がり銘柄数がほぼ拮抗した。

米取引所の合算出来高は１８６億株。直近２０営業日の平均は１７７億株。

item.title: 原油急伸、ブレント一時110ドル 中東・ロシア供給不安で
item.description:
Arathy Somasekhar
[ヒューストン １６日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Arathy Somasekhar

[ヒューストン １６日 ロイター] - 米国時間の原油先物は大幅高となり、北海ブレントが一時１バレル＝１１０ドルと５月以来の高値を付けた。中東情勢の緊迫化で供給が一段と逼迫するとの懸念が広がったほか、ロシアからの世界市場向けディーゼル燃料の供給能力に不透明感が強まったことが背景。

清算値は、北海ブレント先物が３．９４ドル（３．７％）高の１０９．８６ドルで、５月１９日以来の高値。米ＷＴＩ先物は３．４４ドル（３．５％）高の１０１．４１ドルで、９月１７日以来の高値となった。

今週に入ってブレントは４．９％、ＷＴＩは１０．４％、それぞれ上昇した。

FAST

Oct 16 : SoftBank Group is considering an acquisition of Allied Universal in a deal that could value the US security services provider at about $18 billion, a source familiar with the matter said on Friday. • Allied Universal provides security staffing for businesses, venues and major events, and has a growing presence in the data center industry, supporting both development and operation of facilities • The potential acquisition would complement SoftBank founder Masayoshi Son's increasing focus on AI, as he is exploring the use of AI-powered robots across industries, and looking to strengthen the infrastructure needed to support the technology • With Allied, SoftBank would look to eventually replace some staff with robots for certain security tasks, though the deployment of humanoid security workers is likely to take longer.

• Deliberations are preliminary and no final decisions have been made, including on the potential price, Bloomberg News first reported the news • SoftBank declined to comment on the report, while Allied Universal did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment • SoftBank is widely known for making large technology investments through its Vision Fund. It was an early investor in Alibaba, owns a majority stake in Arm, and was a major backer of the office-sharing startup WeWork • The deal builds on SoftBank's broader push into robotics and automation, following its agreement last year to acquire swiss engineering group ABB's robotics business for $5.4 billion

item.description: トランプ氏、スターリンク巡る責任否定 ゼレンスキー氏との関係「良好」 Reuters

item.title: トランプ氏、スターリンク巡る責任否定 ゼレンスキー氏との関係「良好」
item.description: ［ワシントン １６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ワシントン　１６日　ロイター］ - トランプ米大統領は１６日、ウクライナ軍が使う米スペースＸ＜SPCX.O＞の衛星通信サービス「スターリンク」の利用制限が伝えらられたことについて、自身と同社を率いるイーロン・マスク氏のいずれにも責任はないとの認識を示した。

また、ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領と自身の関係は良好だと述べた。

スターリンクを巡っては、ウクライナ軍の司令部との通信が途絶したほか、接続速度も低下したと伝えられている。ロイターは１５日、ホワイトハウスがスターリンクの軍事向けサービス「スターシールド」のサービス縮小を承認したと報じていた。

トランプ氏は記者団に対し、ウクライナのスターリンクを巡る件について自身とマスク氏のいずれも責任はないとの認識を表明。ウクライナによるスターシールドへのアクセス制限については、米国が課したものではないと述べた。

トランプ氏は１５日放映のニュースマックスのインタビューで、ゼレンスキー氏とロシアのプーチン大統領が互いを憎んでいることが戦争終結を難しくしているとの見方を改めて表明。「私はゼレンスキー氏をあまり好んでいない」とした上で「両者とも終結を望んでいると思うが、私はプーチン氏よりもゼレンスキー氏の方が交渉しにくいと感じている」と述べていた。

item.title: Aluminum heads for surplus in 2027 as supply shock fades
item.description: Aluminium is expected to swing into a surplus in 2027, potentially of more than 1 million metric tons, as analysts eye a wave of new supply from Indonesia a
item.dc:creator: Mining.com
item.content:encoded: Aluminium is expected to swing into a surplus in 2027, potentially of more than 1 million metric tons, as analysts eye a wave of new supply from Indonesia and a recovery in flows from Gulf smelters. Expectations for a supply bump have already helped push prices of the metal used in transport and packaging below $3,000 a ton this week to their lowest since December, after they hit four-year highs in June on trade disruptions from the Iran war and dwindling inventories. “We expect a substantial rebound in Middle East supply, with output rising to 6.4 million tons from 4.8 million tons this year,” Ross Strachan, head of aluminium raw materials at CRU, said. The Middle East, which accounts for around 9% of global primary aluminium capacity, has seen shipments severely disrupted by the Iran war. CRU sees a 1.4 million-ton surplus next year, compared to a deficit of 711,000 tons this year. The world produced 73.8 million tons of primary aluminum in 2025. In Indonesia, where projects led by Chinese investors — unable to expand in their home market due to a capacity ceiling — are ramping up, CRU expects output to more than double from this year to 3.2 million tons in 2027. Growing pains Other analysts assume lower surpluses, cautioning that extra supply will be hard-won. Uday Patel, senior research manager at Wood Mackenzie, projects oversupply of around 500,000 tons next year against a 900,000-ton deficit this year. Gulf smelters are recovering but have been forced to use alternative routes to get their metal to export markets, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz at great expense. “You could see a situation where you have a surplus but still elevated premiums and potentially prices,” Patel said. He sees around 1 million tons of additional production from Indonesia next year but points to “growing pains” in the country’s aluminium sector. “The smelters are being built quicker than the infrastructure,” he said, with ports and power supply struggling to keep up. Bank of America commodity strategist Michael Widmer notes that the market had previously expected Indonesia to produce more than 2 million tons of aluminium this year, whereas the actual number could be closer to 1.2 million tons. “It’s coming, but slower than people thought,” said Widmer, who estimates 2.2 million tons of Indonesian supply next year — most of it in the second half — and a smaller surplus of 239,000 tons. (Reporting by Tom Daly; Editing by Jan Harvey)

item.title: 米財政赤字、26年度1.99兆ドルに拡大 5年ぶり高水準
item.description: [１６日 ロイター] - 米財務省が１６日発表した２０２６会計年度（２０２５年１０月─２６年９月）の米連邦政府の財政赤字...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米財政赤字、26年度1.99兆ドルに拡大　5年ぶり高水準 10/17 4:31 配信

2026年7月11日、米財務省庁舎。REUTERS/Daniel Heuer/File Photo/File Photo

[１６日 ロイター] - 米財務省が１６日発表した２０２６会計年度（２０２５年１０月─２６年９月）の米連邦政府の財政赤字は、前年度比２１７０億ドル増の１兆９９００億ドルとなり、５年ぶりの高水準を記録した。関税の還付や、４０兆ドルを超える政府債務の利払い費が過去最高となったことなどが赤字拡大につながった。

社会保障制度向け支出が引き続き増加したことや、国防費が４８０億ドル増加したことも赤字拡大の一因となった。

２６年度はトランプ米大統領の２期目で初めて通年となる会計年度。２５年度の赤字は１兆７８００億ドルだった。２６年度の赤字は、新型コロナウイルス禍への対策支出で２兆７７００億ドルに膨らんだ２１年度以来の規模で、過去３番目の大きさとなった。

２６年度の歳入は過去最高の５兆４０００億ドルで、２５年度の５兆２４００億ドルから１６９０億ドル（３％）増加した。歳出も過去最高の７兆４０００億ドルとなり、前年度の７兆０１００億ドルから３８６０億ドル（６％）増えた。

債務の利払い費は１４４０億ドル（１２％）増の１兆３６００億ドルと、過去最高を記録した。歳出項目別では、社会保障と、高齢者向け公的医療保険「メディケア」・低所得者向け公的医療保険「メディケイド」の合計に次ぐ規模となった。米政府債務は約２カ月前に４０兆ドルを突破した。

関税の純収入が２２０億ドル減少したことも赤字拡大の要因となった。最高裁は２６年、トランプ氏が就任１年目に導入した関税の大部分を無効とする判断を下した。これを受けて同年中に１４５０億ドルの関税還付が行われ、関税の純収入は１１％減の約１７３０億ドルとなった。

２６年度の国防費は６％増の９１７０億ドルだった。財務省当局者は、この増加分のうちイラン戦争に起因する額は明確でないと述べた。

財務省当局者は、２６年度の財政赤字の対国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）比を６．２％と推計したと述べたが、算出に用いたＧＤＰの推計値は明らかにしなかった。２５年度の実績は５．８％だった。

２６年度の最終月に当たる９月の財政収支は２７０億ドルの赤字。前年同月は１９８０億ドルの黒字だった。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：米国の「軽油ショック」、消費者の身の回りで着実に進行 アングル：米国債、投資家はより高いリターンを要求 アングル：金の長期上昇トレンド失速、米利上げ観測とドル高響く アングル：米連邦債務の増加、ウォーシュ次期ＦＲＢ議長の保有資産圧縮計画を制約も コラム：逆風の米財政、イラン紛争で新たな試練に直面 最終更新: 10/17(土) 4:31 ロイター

item.title: ＮＹ外為市場＝ドル軟調、ＦＲＢ金利据え置き観測強まる ＡＩ株安も重し
item.description: ［ニューヨーク １６日 ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場では、ドルが円やユーロなどの主要通貨に対して下落した。米連邦...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ外為市場＝ドル軟調、ＦＲＢ金利据え置き観測強まる　ＡＩ株安も重し 10/17 4:25 配信

２０１１年１月撮影　REUTERS/Kacper Pempel

［ニューヨーク　１６日　ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場では、ドルが円やユーロなどの主要通貨に対して下落した。米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の追加利上げ観測の後退に加え、ＡＩ（人工知能）関連銘柄主導の株安への懸念が引き続き重しになっている。

米国では今週発表された９月の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）と９月の卸売物価指数（ＰＰＩ）をが予想を上回って伸びたことなどで、一時的に利上げ観測が再燃。ただその後、ＦＲＢ当局者の発言で追加利上げを急がない姿勢が示されたことで、ドル相場に対する支援材料も薄れていた。

今週はこのほか、ＡＩ関連銘柄が大幅に下落。ＡＩ関連銘柄やサプライチェーン全体に資金を投じてきた投資家の間でデータセンター運営企業が債務返済に必要な利益を十分なタイミングで確保できるのか疑念が広がっていることが背景にあり、影響はドル相場にも波及している。

ストーンＸのグローバル市場調査責任者、マット・ウェラー氏は「今週、最も興味深いと感じたのはドル相場がＡＩ関連取引と極めて密接に連動したことだった」と指摘。「通常なら、ハイテク株が売られれば安全資産としてドルが買われる展開が予想される。実際、債券市場ではそうした安全資産買いの動きが一部見られたが、ドルはむしろ売られた」と述べた。

ウォーシュＦＲＢ議長はバンコクで開かれた国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）・世界銀行年次総会で行った講演で、米経済の力強さについて楽観的な見方を示すとともに、エネルギーショックが続きインフレ抑制に向けた金融引き締めが行われる中でも、世界経済が持ちこたえていることに驚きを表明。ＦＲＢの金融政策については「予断を持たない」と述べるにとどめ、追加利上げの可能性について手掛かりは示さなかった。

ＢＮＹ（ニューヨーク）の米州担当マクロストラテジスト、ジョン・ベリス氏は「２７─２８日の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）での利上げについて、ＦＯＭＣ内で特に理事の間で十分な支持があるとは思えない」と指摘。「１２月の次回会合については結論はまだ出ていない。それまでに多くのことが起こり得る」と述べた。

ＣＭＥフェドウオッチによると、今月の会合で金利据え置きが決定される確率は８３％。１カ月前の４９％から大きく上昇した。

終盤の取引で、ドル／円は０．０８％安の１ドル＝１５８．１１円。日銀の植田和男総裁は１６日、基調的な物価上昇率について、２％に「かなり近づいている」と指摘する一方で、２％目標に到達したかの判断は２９日からの金融政策決定会合で「政策委員の間でしっかり議論して結論を出したい」と述べるにとどめた。

ユーロ／ドルは０．０８％高の１．１２２７ドル。

主要６通貨に対するドル指数は０．１７％安の１０１．８７。

ドル／円　ＮＹ終値 157.99/158.04

始値 157.89

高値 158.33

安値 157.70

ユーロ／ドル　ＮＹ終値 1.1239/1.1240

始値 1.1258

高値 1.1261

安値 1.1213

item.content:encoded:
欧州市場サマリー（16日） 10/17 4:15 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞

続伸して取引を終えた。ＦＴＳＥ１００種は３日続伸。週間ベースでは３．１３％高で、上昇率は約半年ぶりの大きさだった。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は前日比０．４５％高、週間では１．３２％上昇した。

英政権の財政規律重視の予算編成方針が好感され、週間ベースでＦＴＳＥ３５０種住宅建設株指数は６．４８％高。飲料株指数は７．７５％、ヘルスケア株指数は５．４８％それぞれ上昇した。

ブリティッシュ・アメリカン・タバコは前日比２．１％高。酒造大手のディアジオは１．９％上昇した。

銀行株指数は、銀行への課税の可能性が伝えられ、下落した。

航空宇宙・防衛株指数は０．４５％高。防衛大手ＢＡＥシステムズは２．６％、バブコック・インターナショナルは３．６％それぞれ上昇した。

通期利益見通しを引き上げた電子商取引（ＥＣ）大手ＴＨＧは１０．８％高だった。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞

続伸して取引を終えた。堅調な企業業績を受けて買い注文が優勢だった。ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種指数は週間ベースでは２．０９％上昇した。

ＬＳＥＧのＩＢＥＳのデータによると、ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種の構成企業全体の２０２６年７─９月期の利益は、前年同期比２０．７％増と見込まれている。

堅調な受注が確認されたドイツの半導体製造装置メーカー、アイクストロンは前日比６．２％高。通期の利益率見通しを引き上げたドイツの風力タービンメーカー、ノルデックスは１２．３％高。一方、配電・制御機器大手シュナイダー・エレクトリックは１．８％安。

ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種テクノロジー株指数は０．０６％高。週間では３．３９％下落した。

食品・飲料株指数は前日比１．３７％高。ＪＰモルガンが投資判断を引き上げたスイスの食品大手ネスレは１．７％上昇した。

一方、ヘルスケア株指数は０．２５％安だった。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞

域内国債利回りが横ばいで推移した。ただ、人工知能（ＡＩ）関連企業が巨額支出に見合うリターンを上げられるかどうかへの懸念から、国債には安全資産として買いが入っており、週間ベースでは低下の見通しとなった。

今週初め、ＡＩ関連投資に絡み債務が膨らんだ企業の株式・社債が大きく売られたことが、株式市場全般の重しとなり、投資家は国債に回帰した。世界の国債市場は週間ベースでは４カ月ぶりの大幅上昇に向かっており、ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、主要７カ国（Ｇ７）の国債利回りは平均で８．７ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）低下の４．２７３％となった。

ソシエテ・ジェネラルのアナリストは「ＡＩブームを巡る懸念が国債の投資妙味を高めている」と指摘。ただ、「こうした局面は過去にもあった」とした上で、これがＡＩ投資に対する熱狂やサイクルの終わりを意味するとは思わないとの見方を示した。

ユーロ圏の指標金利であるドイツの１０年債利回りは１ｂｐ上昇し、３．４２％前後で推移した。ただ、週間では約７ｂｐ低下した。

欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）の政策金利見通しに敏感な独２年債利回りは２ｂｐ低下の３．０６％となった。

ここ数週間で最も大きく売られてきたフランス１０年債利回りは４．７９％前後と横ばいで推移した。週間では７ｂｐ低下と、８月序盤以来の低下幅となる見通し。財政問題に対処する仏政府の能力を巡り、市場では根深い懸念が広がっている。

独仏１０年債利回り格差は約１３７ｂｐ。今月２日には約１６０ｂｐと１５年ぶりの高水準を付けていた。

市場は、今月のＥＣＢ理事会で利上げが実施されるとの見方は織り込んでいないものの、１２月には１００％の確率で利上げが行われると予想。来年４月までに少なくとももう１回追加利上げに踏み切るとみている。

item.title: ローマ教皇、プーチン氏とウ占領地の人道支援協力で合意 入院中に電話会談
item.description:
Joshua McElwee
[バチカン市国 １６日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Joshua McElwee

[バチカン市国　１６日　ロイター] - ロシアのプーチン大統領は、ローマ教皇レオ１４世が１６日の電話会談で、ロシア占領下にあるウクライナ南部ヘルソン州オレシキに緊急物資を搬入するための協力を求めたのに対し、協力することで合意したと伝えた。ロシア大統領府（クレムリン）が明らかにした。

教皇庁（バチカン）によると、教皇はプーチン氏に電話し、オレシキへの救援物資や食料の搬入を可能にするため停戦を要請するとともに、同地の人道状況について「深い懸念」を表明した。

クレムリンは声明で「町の住民の安全を確保し、必要な物資供給を組織するために必要な環境を整える取り組みを支援するというバチカンの意向を支持した」とした上で、「この件に関して協力することで合意した」と表明。ただ、停戦については言及しなかった。

教皇は１３日に肺がん切除の手術を受けた後、ローマのジェメッリ病院で療養中。バチカンは１６日、教皇の容体は着実に改善しており、仕事や通常の日常生活をこなせる状態にあると明らかにしていた。

item.title: U.S. Treasury Department’s investigation does not signal reduced bond issuance; U.S. Treasury yields rise as 10-year reclaims 5.12%
item.description: In a survey soliciting opinions from primary dealers, the Treasury Department asked about plans for repurchasing long-term government bonds, ways to enhance repo efficiency, the timing of short-term bond issuance, and prospects for the economy and financing, but did not directly address the issue of reducing long-term bond supply. Some investors had expected the Treasury to use this questionnaire to more clearly signal that it is considering scaling back the size of long-term bond auctions or even stopping the issuance of 20-year bonds, in response to the Trump administration's efforts to lower financing costs. The refinancing announcement to be released by the Treasury on November 4 has become the next observation point.
item.dc:creator: 华尔街见闻
item.content:encoded: The latest primary dealer survey by the U.S. Treasury did not provide a clear signal that it will imminently cut the size of long-term Treasury auctions, disappointing investors who were betting on government action to suppress long-term interest rates. As a result, U.S. Treasuries fell and yields generally rose. This survey is part of the Treasury's preparation for the quarterly refunding plan to be announced on November 4. The market had hoped to find clues from the questionnaire about whether Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen might adjust the size of long-term Treasury issuance, especially the much-discussed possibility of reducing or even halting the issuance of 20-year bonds. However, the Treasury only broadly asked what auction scale adjustments should be considered in the future, without explicitly suggesting that a supply cut for long-term debt is imminent. After the release of the Treasury's survey, U.S. Treasury yields rose across the board in the secondary market. The U.S. 10-year benchmark Treasury yield climbed back to 5.12%, approaching the day's pre-market high of 5.1315%, with the intraday gain expanding again to 6.5 basis points; the 20-year Treasury yield rose 5.4 basis points on the day, and the 30-year yield saw its intraday increase expand again to about 5 basis points. The 2-year yield erased its intraday decline and turned higher. Meanwhile, oil prices had already begun rising shortly before the survey was released, also adding upward pressure to U.S. Treasury yields. Therefore, Friday's yield rise reflected both disappointment that the Treasury failed to deliver a supply-reduction signal and the influence of changes in energy prices. What Did the Treasury Ask, and What Is the Market Waiting For? This time, the Treasury solicited opinions from primary dealers, focusing on what adjustments to Treasury auction sizes should be considered in the face of structural changes in investor demand, and with the expectation that medium-term demand may continue to evolve in the future. Such surveys are routine preparatory work for the Treasury’s quarterly refunding decisions, aimed at understanding the main dealers' assessments of government financing needs, investor demand, and market conditions, to inform the final determination of Treasury issuance scale and structure. The survey itself is not a funding plan, nor does it mean the Treasury has decided to adjust issuance sizes for any maturities. According to reports, this questionnaire also covered multiple debt management topics: Long-term Treasury Buyback Program: The Treasury asked whether expanding the size of long-term Treasury buybacks has improved market liquidity and trading operations; how larger buybacks would affect dealers' ability to fulfill client orders, and clients’ willingness to participate directly or indirectly in buybacks. Further Improving Buyback Efficiency: The Treasury solicited suggestions from dealers on what further adjustments could be made to the buyback program. T-Bills and Floating Rate Note Issuance Timing: The Treasury asked whether it should change the current practice of avoiding issuing T-bills and floating rate notes on FOMC rate decision days. Economic and Financing Outlook: Dealers also need to provide forecasts regarding the economy, fiscal and monetary policy, and the Treasury’s borrowing needs for the coming fiscal years. What really disappointed the market was that the Treasury did not directly address the issue of reducing long-term Treasury supply. Some investors had hoped that the Treasury would use this questionnaire to more clearly signal it is considering downsizing long-term bond auctions, or even halting 20-year bond issuance, in response to efforts (advocated by the Trump administration) to lower financing costs. Blake Gwinn, Head of U.S. Rates Strategy at RBC Capital Markets, said if the Treasury intended to send a signal or influence yields via the survey, it could have asked much more direct questions. He believes this survey conveyed no substantial signals; given that some investors expected significant adjustments such as discontinuing the 20-year bond, the outcome may have disappointed the market. 20-Year Bond in Focus, Wall Street Bets on Treasury Adjusting Issuance Structure The market is extremely sensitive to this survey, mainly because long-term Treasury yields have been high recently. With the persistent U.S. fiscal deficit and growing interest payments on existing debt, government financing needs are on the rise. Pressure from long-term Treasury supply has become a core concern for investors. According to Bloomberg, some Wall Street institutions previously bet that the Treasury might ease long-term bond supply pressure by adjusting issuance structure. The focus of discussion has especially been on the 20-year bond: whether the Treasury would cut its issuance size or even abolish this maturity outright. From a financing mechanism perspective, the Treasury must meet the government's overall borrowing needs but does not have to issue each maturity type in fixed proportions. If there is sufficient demand and market capacity for short-term instruments, in theory, the Treasury could boost short-term debt issuance and thus reduce supply pressures in the long-term bond market. However, adjusting maturity structure also changes the government’s future refinancing needs and cannot simply be interpreted as reducing total borrowing. Molly Brooks, U.S. Rates Strategist at TD Securities, said the Treasury’s questions are still too general and do not explicitly ask whether to reduce long-term bond supply, hence the disappointment in the market. She expects any adjustment to long-term bond auction sizes is unlikely before February 2027 at the earliest. This means the optimistic scenario that some investors had bet on—where the Treasury would announce cuts to long-term issuance, or even eliminate the 20-year bond, in the November quarterly refunding plan—may not materialize soon. The questionnaire did not provide a clear supply-reduction signal, nor does it rule out potential future adjustments. Issuance Signal Disappoints, Oil Price Surge Adds to Long-End Yield Pressure Beyond the Treasury’s survey, rising oil prices have also added upward pressure on Treasury yields. Higher energy prices could reignite inflation concerns and affect investors’ views of the future path of Fed interest rates. For longer-dated Treasuries, inflation expectations, future short-term rates, and required term premiums all influence yield pricing. This also explains why the market reaction was concentrated in long-dated Treasuries. Long-term bond prices are especially sensitive to changes in supply expectations: if investors were expecting the Treasury to reduce long-end issuance and such signals are missing, they may reassess both the amount of long-term bonds they must hold and the returns they demand for taking on interest rate risk. However, it would be wrong to attribute Friday’s rise in yields solely to the Treasury survey. Changes in oil prices were also highlighted as a driver in reports; the survey results merely fell short of the market’s hopes for a more proactive policy shift, and do not directly prove that the scale of future long-term Treasury issuance will remain unchanged. November 4 Refund Announcement Becomes the Next Focal Point The Treasury will announce the next quarterly refunding plan on November 4, at which point the market will be able to further assess the government's views on borrowing needs, issuance sizes for different maturities, and the specifics of buyback arrangements. The U.S. government faces persistent budget deficits, and interest on existing debt is also rising, which means the Treasury must strike a balance among financing costs, market demand, and the maturity structure of debt. Cutting long-term supply to lower long-end yields is one possible path the market is watching, but it is not without constraints. Before the formal announcement, dealer surveys are only market consultations and not policy commitments. The drop in long-end Treasury prices and renewed rise in yields on Friday reflected that the market was originally hoping for a more proactive supply-reduction signal from the Treasury, which was not sufficiently evident in the survey. Going forward, investors will continue to watch whether the Treasury adjusts its long-end issuance plans in the November refunding, and whether such moves can truly alleviate the supply pressure on long-term Treasuries.
